item.title: Weekly Parsha Points VaYishlach (“He sent”) Are You Authentic?
item.description: Part Two
item.content:encoded:
Audio edition of Weekly Parsha Points VaYishlach (“He sent”) Are You Authentic? on Contender's Voice. For more, visit contendersvoice.com.

Book of Genesis

VaYishlach (“He sent”)

Are You Authentic ?

Part 2

Seek Him

There are several more beneficial life lessons we can glean from the story of Jacob’s return to Canaan. They are: 1. Human plans and efforts alone do not bring to pass, or prevent from coming to pass, Elohim’s prophetic purposes or plans. 2. It can be said that Jacob represents the people of Elohim today [disciples of Yeshua] who are appointed unto victory in the earth. 3. Furthermore, it is Elohim, our holy Creator, who is faithful to watch over His elect. The Almighty (a) produces our successes and (b) brings to pass in our lives the needed victories for each of us, as they, even in a small way, reflect the theme of restitution of all things spoken by the prophets.

Make yourself ready!

Note: As you know, blessed reader, the “restoration of all things” (Acts 3:21) occurs when Messiah Yeshua returns to earth and establishes His Kingdom. The Second-coming advent will restore Earth itself to a greater glory, beauty, and productivity, et al, than that even of Eden. His Word clearly notifies us! “Let us rejoice and be glad and give Him glory! For the wedding of the Lamb has come, and His betrothed bride [wife] has made herself ready” (Revelation 19:7). She is not preoccupied with spa dainties or appearing lovely to the world–rather, she belongs to Messiah and seeks first to please Him alone.

No snoozfest for the saints.

Note: Zechariah 4:6 reminds us with what is written: “...not by [your] might nor by [your] power, but by my Spirit, says the Lord of Hosts.” Be sure, friend: We must remain dependent upon Him in order to depart from unprofitable busyness and turn to accomplishing our assignments and developing our generational legacies–which will follow us into eternity. Hence, effectual, prevailing prayer, is that splendid time to which we must resort daily. Learn: First, effectual, prevailing prayer is an act of faith practiced by Jacob. Next, it is the persistent prayer of importuning. Finally, it is the prayer of intense, earnest desire. Remember Jacob’s words: “I will not let you go, except you bless me.” And let it be said, it is the prayer that readily moves the heart and hand of the Almighty. So commit to a recalibrated prayer life and importune day by day. No let up!

Journey forward.

When believers are on the road of Elohim’s commandments and making our way to a better country, the Kingdom of Heaven–-we may experience helpful divine visitations/encounters as did many of our single-minded forefathers in the faith. Pray to receive them. Elohim is not a respecter of persons. Repent, turn to His Word, consecrate your life. Do not compromise. It’s an enemy. A visitation of His glory can do more for and in a believer–such as transform, deliver, empower, and enlighten…in just a few moments than much time spent in ordinary religious training. Scripture is full of such divine occurrences. Therefore,saint, sanctify your self, exalt Yeshua, and do not stop moving forward in you journey to eternity and the Father’s heavenly abode. .

Make yourself ready for His coming!

Opening in 2027

Torah and Glory School

1. Subscribe: Your sponsorship of Contenders Weekly Parsha Points and the coming monthly Torah and Glory School and Spiritual Restoration Report, would be much appreciated. Weekly parsha readings of God’s Word from the Torah, the Prophets, and the New Covenant are read around the world. They and the YGS are ministries of Contenders Voice. Contendersvoice.com.

2. Carefully review our Torah and Glory Schools presentation on our Contenders Voice website. Construction for our Torah and Glory School is almost completed. This school is one year long and consists of five parts. Further, TGS is a college level undertaking that requires vision, faith, and determination to complete. The program is ideal for small home groups. Its purpose: To equip earnest, knowledgeable disciples of Yeshua who will also emerge to make disciples themselves. Our goal is to develop faith teams led and empowered by His Spirit for Latter Day service. For more information on Torah and Glory schools visit and review our Contenders Voice Website. See: Contendersvoice.com

Ideal for the home, small discipleship groups...and for You!

TGS classes are not casual Bible studies where people come and go at leisure. TGS is set to be a demanding Spirit and Torah year-long education ministry of Contenders Voice that requires faith, vision, and sustained effort. Reason for Being: 1. To equip and raise up disciples for Yeshua, and train them to also become disciples-makers also. 2. To restore all the ministries of the Holy Spirit and Torah truth to the westernized Body of

Messiah.

Tamid Kadima–Always Forward. Hutch Church, your host. Thank you, blessed readers following Contenders Parsha Points. Enjoy total well being in every area of your life. And be with Yeshua. True worship–compliance to his teaching, will transform you. Shalom.

item.title: Weekly Parsha Points - VaYishlach (“He sent”) — Are You Authentic?
item.description: Book of Genesis VaYishlach (“He sent”) Are You Authentic ? Part 1 Last week, in parsha VaYetzei , we read about Jacob leaving his comfortable home and familiar surroundings in Beersheba to go forth to Padan-aram in Mesopotamia, and visit…
item.content:encoded:
Audio edition of Weekly Parsha Points - VaYishlach (“He sent”) — Are You Authentic? on Contender's Voice. For more, visit contendersvoice.com.

Book of Genesis

VaYishlach (“He sent”)

Are You Authentic ?

Part 1

Last week, in parsha VaYetzei, we read about Jacob leaving his comfortable home and familiar surroundings in Beersheba to go forth to Padan-aram in Mesopotamia, and visit his parents’ relatives. In doing so, Jacob was taking his first steps toward fulfilling his destiny and becoming spiritually transformed in the process.

Real followers pass the test.

Central truth: The Father loves us too much to allow us to remain in the same spiritual place and condition for long, or settle back in familiar but unprofitable comfort zones. He wants us to continue to grow stronger in faith and move unto deeper and more intimate fellowship with Him. Our Messiah spoke to His disciples in this way: “If you abide [ obey, endure, stay in place] in my word, you are truly my disciples.” Understand: What this phrase, “truly my disciples” implies is that there are disciples who are not truly disciples. The word “truly” means “really”--as in ”really my disciples.” In any case, it has been said that a life without duty, discipline, or commitment, i.e. purpose, is bereft of satisfaction and joy. Do you agree?

Created for good works.

In other words there are real and unreal disciples who do not conform to or care about the teaching of Yeshua. There are both authentic and inauthentic disciples in the Church. The imposters are not led by the Holy Spirit. Consider: There is discipleship that is merely outward (a big show), and a discipleship that is faith-filled, inspirational, and completely sincere. So, to which group do you really belong, dear reader. “If you abide [obey] in My Word” is the test. Genuine disciples have eternity in their vision and are positioned for victory and blessing as they grow into overcomers and mature as the Bride of Messiah. See Revelation 2 and 3.

Steps to Discipleship.

This week, in parsha VaYishlach, we read the record of Jacob’s flight from Padan-aram back to Beersheba. However, it appears that his eventful return did not go quite as he had envisioned. The report of his troubled trek back to Canaan could be given this way: “A man’s heart devises the way; but the LORD directs his steps” (Proverbs 16:9). This is very good news for all attentive believers, wouldn’t you say?

The reminder applies to the Christian believers of this age, and also to the descendants of the scattered tribes of the House of Israel who are endeavoring to return to and settle into their Hebraic, Torah-based heritage. This is the birthright blessing attained by believers through their faith in Messiah Yeshua as Savior and sole Mediator of the New Covenant. Hebrews 8:6;12:24. But be informed. Modern saints have been called to contend for [recover and restore] the Torah and Spirit rooted faith that was once delivered to the apostolic, New Covenant Judean Ecclesia (Kahal). Over the centuries however, this faith been compromised, vitiated, and broken apart by false teachings and wandering religious orthodoxies. Determination and endurance are the pre-requisites for recovering the original New Testament apostolic faith and abiding in its truth. This presents a duty to modern disciples.

Parsha VaYishlach (“He sent’)

References: Genesis 32:3-36:43; Hosea 11:7-12:12; Joshua 11:5-19; First Corinthians 5:1-13; Revelation 7:1-12.

Apply the features of Jacob’s journey to your own.

We cannot cover in detail the complete narrative of this rich parsha in our “Points” briefing. However, we will glean relevant lessons from the narrative of Jacob’s journey home to Beersheba. Dear reader, you will be inspired by witnessing his climatic spiritual transformation which occurred during his eventful trek homeward. Goal: Start abiding in the light of divine truth known to you just as the patriarch did when he set out on his arduous journey. You will learn that no matter what resistance or trials you encounter, as you honor Yahweh you will be become transformed as well, but into your Savior’s likeness. Such is a wonderful opportunity, and privilege! Hence it is written: “Trust in YHWH with all thine heart and lean not on your own understanding. In all your ways acknowledge Him and He shall direct your paths” (Proverbs 3:5-6). So, let’s consider the following six points.

Providential Oversight.

  1. 1. “...return to the land of your fathers..“ (Gen, 31:3). After twenty years of serving his father-in-law Laban in Padam-aram, Yahweh directed Jacob to return to Canaan, the land of his father Abraham. And Jacob went, taking his family and flocks with him, and Yahweh’s reassuring promises, such as: ”I will be with you.” Such an affirmation would be hugely encouraging to any traveler. We have ours too, as we walk the narrow spoken of by Yeshua! Remember Matthew 28:16-20 and Joshua 1:9. Notwithstanding, Jacob left Padan-aram but shortly afterwards was confronted by Laban who pursued him. Their issues were settled with a covenant. Learn: Trust in your Father’s faithfulness and compassionate care, friend, concerning any confrontation or circumstance that suddenly comes upon you.

A heavenly escort. How good is that?

2. “...the angels of God met him“ (32:1). Jacob continued southward to the Jabbok River where heavenly angels, the messengers of Almighty God, intercepted him [fell in with him]. He was informed by his new escort service that Esau was nearby, and to be prepared. Note: This encounter was not just a vision, it was a supernatural manifestation of heavenly ministers. Jacob recognized them as God’s host–or Mananeh. Learn: A heavenly escort is an emblem of angelic guardianship which “encampeth round about them that fear [reverence and trust] the LORD and delivereth them…” and “..keepeth them in all their ways” (Psalms 34 and 91). That includes you, dear reader. You are highly valued and your faith journey is being chaperoned by a heaavenly escort, even now!

Be courageous and strong. Be not dismayed or afraid.

3. “Then the messengers returned...“ (32:6). Having learned of Esau’s approach, Jacob “...sent messengers before him to his brother Esau in the land of Seir, the country of Edom’” (B’resheit 32:3). They returned to inform the weary traveler that his brother had 400 armed men with him. Jacob feared violent consequences could occur during this “reunion” so he acted quickly and wisely. The dutiful patriarch divided his family and flocks into two camps behind him. And he prayed, “Oh God of my father Abraham and God of my father Isaac, Oh LORD…deliver me I pray thee”. Jacob prayed with humility and intensity unto YHWH who—as pointed out already, had made wonderful promises to his fathers of which he was the heir. Learn: He says to you personally: “The LORD your God is with you. He is mighty to save. He will take great delight in you, He will quiet you with His love, He will rejoice over you with singing” (Zephaniah 3:17). Reader, hold to your hope.

Give gifts. It Works.

4. “...so he took what came to his hand…” (32:13). Jacob believed the threat he perceived could not actually be reconciled. It appeared to him that the looming rapproachment [the restoration of happy relations] was beyond his ability to handle. So he sought the one who said, “I will surely do good and make your seed as the sand of the sea.” Jacob was given wisdom, the most valuable tool for handling confrontations—i. e., spiritual warfare. Hence, sent a series of gifts–herds and flocks–to soften the temperament of Esau and show respect to his older brother with courteous words, such as referring to him as “my master.” As a result, their meeting was amiable, and after friendly exchanges and assurances they separated. Then Jacob sent his family over the Jabbok tributary but he remained alone. Learn: Kindness and courtesy honor Yahweh and work wonders with your fellow man.

Soft words break bones–stubbornness.

5. “In this manner you shall speak to him…” (32:19). Jacob grew in wisdom and his experience had given him an acute understanding of human nature. He learned that kindness and warm words could soften a hard heart. “I will appease him with a present.” Learn: A repetition of generous presents would act upon Esau in the same way a blacksmith’s hammer, through repeated strikes, shapes the posture of hot iron. There would be a notable effect on the brothers’ reunion by way of Jacob’s wise action–-the fruit of an affectionate reunion. Learn: The Holy One of Israel acknowledges and blesses a generous giver. Remember the poor widow and her two-penny offering? She’s in the Bible’s Hall of Fame for eternity, friend, and rich beyond calculation.

Engage in unrelenting prayer.

6. “Then Jacob was left alone, and a man wrestled with him…” ( 32:22-32). In the verse we witness the mysterious wrestling match between Jacob and a man we interpret to be the visible, physical representation of the invisible Elohim. The confrontation occurred abruptly at a time when Jacob was engrossed in devout, heartfelt prayer. The contest was indeed a physical effort, but foremost it was an intense struggle preoccupying the soul of Jacob. He wanted and needed an enduring blessing, as do many of us today. However, he was given first a dislocated hip, of all thing! Yet Jacob persisted in striving with his heavenly Opponent. Point: Perhaps the dislocated hip was a sign and reminder that Jacob would never succeed in fulfilling his destiny by depending upon his own human strength and carnal temperament. Rather, such would be accomplished only by full reliance on the Almighty. Period. The Contender, allowed Jacob to prevail, and graciously gave him a blessed new name, Israel. It means “one who prevails with God and man.” Learn: Emulate Jacob. Here’s your verse. Live it! “Let us not grow weary in doing good, for in due season we will reap if we don’t give up” (Gal. 6:9). Keep Persevering, blessed reader.

Conclusion of VaYishlach, Part 1

The featured confrontation took place on the north side of the Jabbok river at night where Jacob had been alone, communing in his heart and making supplication and confession. It was at that time of focused prayer the heavenly Visitor suddenly approached him and the physical struggle began. Learn: 1. Set aside an altar time of reading and prayer every day. 2. Increase your attention span. 3. Start listening for His voice. 5. Abide in His Word. Point: Your Elohim, who hears, is bigger than your troubles and stronger than your enemies. He will bless you, reader, according to your need. Therefore, keep seeking his face. Trust His promises. Deepen your relationship with Him, Shaddai–Almighty God—the All Sufficient One. And especially be baptized in the Holy Spirit and Fire. and you will do well. Amen.

Tamid Kadima-Always Forward. Part 2 is next: It points out the lessons coming out

from Shechem from which we can benefit. Let’s go there together and walk together with Jacob. Hutch Church Shalom.

item.title: Parsha Points - Parsha VaYeitzei (“He went out”)
item.description: Personal Transformation. Will you pay the Price?
item.content:encoded:
Audio edition of Parsha Points - Parsha VaYeitzei (“He went out”) on Contender's Voice. For more, visit contendersvoice.com.

Book of Genesis

Parsha VaYeitzei (“He went out”)

Personal Transformation. Will you pay the Price?

Part 2

A life-changing encounter for Jacob.

At night, on his return journey home, Jacob came to the River Jabbok. He sent his large

family across the river and was afterwards left alone. Then, as it is written: “... a man

wrestled with him until the breaking of the day.” How the contest started we are not informed. Nevertheless, when the man saw that he did not prevail against Jacob, he put his hip out of socket as they wrestled. Then he said, “Let me go because the day has broken.” But Jacob said, “I will not let you go until you bless me.” And he said, “What is your name?” And the young sojourner said, “Jacob.” Then he said, “Your name shall no longer be called Jacob, but Israel, for you have striven with God and man and have prevailed.” Genesis 34:24-28. Note: There are several standards to point out that contributed to Jacob’s transformation into a new man, “Israel.” And these points could inspire you as well, reader, depending on your spiritual ambition of course.

1.The reluctance to release his opponent, even when his thigh joint had been dislocated, indicates Jacob’s unwavering determination to be blessed by God in a meaningful and most needed way. Point: Despite circumstances, a modern saint must also persevere in fervent prayer before the Throne of Grace. The believer is instructed to pray always with “all prayer and supplication in the Spirit” (Ephesians 6:18).

2. Jacob was given a new name, Israel. It makes a statement that Jacob was one who would strive with the Almighty until he prevailed. Point: Friend, do likewise! Set your course to excel as an overcomer. Strive with Yahweh to be blessed in this worthy campaign and you will also receive a new name from Yeshua, your High Priest. Revelation 2:17!

3. Jacob was spiritually elevated by the blessing bestowed upon him and came to understand the importance of God’s favor and his need for providential care. Point: Seek to honor Him in all things. Learn to be led and instructed by the Holy Spirit.. Wisdom is a weapon of warfare. Ephesians 1:18!

4. The circumstances of his previous years had changed Jacob, yet the Jabbok River event positioned Jacob in a higher spiritual level altogether. Jacob embraced the true God and His precepts as did His father Isaac, and grandfather, Abraham. [Their instruction likely came from Shem who was alive at that time.] Point: Jacob learned obedience. New Covenant saint, grow up and learn obedience too. There’s no room for hypocrisy in your quest to rank among the blessed overcomers. You may also have divine, life-changing divine encounters with Elohim, your Creator. Expect to hear His voice by the Spirit and encounter His presence in a discernable way. Get baptized in the Holy Spirit. See: Acts 1:1-9 and 2.1-47; 10:44-46; 19:6; 1 Cor. 14.

Follow Yahweh’s truth, not the endless banter humans.

Obedience is not legalism. It is the pure, biblical demonstration of faith and love for our Creator and Redeemer. You and I can spend months – pursuing and engaging political conflicts, advancing technology, assorted ideologies, financial upheavals and their threats, war, and religious inventions and controversies, to cite a few common preoccupations. But all that stuff will, in time, become repetitive and wearisome. Point: As Solomon realized as he drew close to his death, man’s chief duty is to obey God’s sacred Word. Our battle’s core is spiritual–always. If we won’t follow our Master after “His manner,” we will continue to abide under a demonic curse. Selah. 2 Chronicles 7:14 waits to be fiulfilled. “If my people, who are called…” You know the rest. But did you know that without obedience to known, applicable, and doable Scriptural truth there is no real repentance and no true discipleship? Pray. Wait upon the Spirit of Truth to come alongside you. And remember the plight of King Saul.

Peniel:

Did you know that locations can leave an impression on people that causes changes in their world view, stirs introspection, and even inspires personal development. Thus the Almighty chooses appropriate places for His work with people. Jacob named the place of his encounter with the heavenly wrestler, Peniel. The generally accepted meaning of the name is: For I have seen God face to face. However, since no human can see Elohim’s face and live, the name could refer to a close, spiritually intimate interaction. Keep in mind, friend. You can do your own research and decide for yourself concerning anything written in our blogs. This has always been our counsel concerning what Contenders Voice ministries happen to teach.

Note: Following this amazing visitation, an existential work of grace, Jacob went forward fully prepared to meet and be reconciled with his once-hostile brother, Esau.

The Torah is the standard of Discipleship

The study of the Torah is essential for Christians, and everyone else, for that matter. The Torah’s origin is divine, it is not restricted, but has a universal application. “It has been evident that believers, including preachers, often interpret the Bible through the lens of their culture, worldview, and public education. This has resulted in many misleading religious beliefs, doctrines and practices becoming prevalent in the Christianity that are not in accord with the clear and pure teachings of the holy Scriptures. Lamentably, this is often the case with the evangelical church in the United States. This country is strongly influential across the globe. Hence, the American evangelical system has also produced a strong influence worldwide. This has occurred by the exportation of a westernized gospel replete with an American pattern of faith that is not in line with the Hebraic paradigm of Scripture. Consequently, in the United States pulpit preaching usually comes across looking more like “American Dream” and “Self-actualization” lessons than the Torah-based and Spirit-powered Gospel. Unabridged, expository proclamations are what is needed now. VaYetzei’s related three closing points should find applications in your own lives, my persistent friends.

He will visit you.

Point 1. “Jacob departed…and encountered a place and spent the night there…” (10-11). The location of Jacob’s encounter with Yeshua was Mount Moriah, the site where Abraham bound Isaac on the altar and where the Temple would later stand. Point: For disciples to desire a visitation of the Holy One of Israel is biblical. Learn: Jacob is a type of each one of us who is awakening and coming to our biblical heritage. The ladder in his dream is seen as Yeshua’s cross of atonement which was situated on earth and still reaches into heaven, for it was the divine mediator who was sacrificed upon it. He now stands above the cross and speaks to the heirs of salvation–His chosen: “I will never leave you.” Point: In our own journeys to our prescribed destinies may our daily times of prayer, praise, study, and service result in divine encounters with Elohim at the gate of glory. Moses pleaded :“Please show me your glory.” Yahweh responds: “I will do this very thing you have asked…” (Exodus 33:18). Moses had found favor in God’s sight. WHY? What’s your answer?

You are sent also. What is your purpose?

Point 2. “And he went out…” Jacob’s life teaches attentive believers that each of us has

a familiar past, an old life, a family and even a religion of some sort from which we must separate in order to go forward and accept the challenge of pursuing Yahweh’s prophetic truth and make our own contribution to the restoration of all things spoken of by the prophets–including both the houses of Israel. Learn: When Jacob went out to face his tests of faith and pursue his destiny, Elohim’s voice spoke to him, personally assuring Jacob that the Most High Elohim would be in continual attendance with him in his pilgrimage just as He was with his fathers. Point: As Jacob was sent by Isaac, each saint today has been sent forth by their Good Shepherd, Yeshua. “Go ye therefore…and I am with you…” (Matthew 28:18-20).

Transformative, purifying Holy Fire

Point 3. Reader, you have a heavenly Helper! Yield to His leading. It is written: “But when he, the Spirit of Truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth: for he will not speak of himself; but whatsoever he shall hear, that shall he speak: and he will show you things to come” (John 16:3). Learn: For New Testament saints to be changed from a Jacob into an Israel we need an internal spiritual fire. Hence, every saint would do well to be baptized by Yeshua with the Holy Spirit, as I mentioned earlier. This experience is a gift that (1) gives power and (2) enhances faith and zeal for the recipients to live for Yeshua and follow His instructions.

Get Zeal !

Our High Priest, Yeshua, is the Kingdom’s Lawgiver. Some of His modern saints are beginning to love the Father’s precepts, judgments, testimonies, statutes, and commandments exceedingly. It is fitting. Point: Because of their faith in and love for their Shepherd, His followers (sheep) want to live zealously by His laws and standards, i.e., boldly follow His instructions. See Romans 16:25-26; Hebrews 10:16).

Cross over to New Wine

One of Jacob’s “life lessons” shows us that although each believer in Messiah Yeshua has a familiar past, an old life, a family, or even a religion, we must separate from old, unholy influences. This is called sanctification--being set apart for Yahweh purposes. It is necessary for advancing forward and meeting the challenge of pursuing Yahweh’s prophetic word. Our call is to make a contribution to the restoration of all things spoken of by the prophets (Acts 3:21). When Jacob left his family and went out to face his tests of faith and pursue his destiny, Elohim spoke to him, personally. Jacob was assured that the Most High would be in continual attendance with him in his pilgrimage, just as He was with his fathers. Point: As Jacob was sent by Isaac, each New Covenant, Spirit-born believer in Yeshua is sent also, and accompanied by His Spirit. It is written: “He will not let your foot slip–he who watches over you will not slumber” (Psalm 121:3-4). Therefore, reader, cast your anxieties on Him. He cares for you. So go forward on your faith pathway to spiritual maturity. Review Matthew 28:18-20; Hebrews 6:1-3.

Our job: Teach His people to obey His precepts and judgments.

It is the Messiah’s will that the truth, standards, and principles of His Law [His teaching; instructions for life and worship] would be fulfilled in the lives of His followers (Romans 3:31; 8:4). Understand: Our High Priest, Yeshua, is the Kingdom’s Lawgiver. His modern saints are awakening spiritually and beginning to love the Father’s precepts, judgments, testimonies, statutes, and commandments exceedingly. It is fitting. Point: Because of their faith in and love for their Shepherd, His followers (sheep) want to live by His laws and standards, i.e., to follow His instructions. See Romans 16:25-26 and Hebrews 10:16. This is His way!

We will continue to study Jacob’s life in greater detail in the next five parshas of Genesis by highlighting its most relevant features. It is profitable to first understand how the patriarch’s life, social status, and prophetic family vision relate to that of believers today–which includes you and myself, your Parsha Points host. Next week’s Parsha is VaYishlach (“And he sent”). Its narrative covers Jacob and his family’s flight from Beersheba to Padan-aram. We will glean helpful, personally advantageous lessons from this parsha.

Until next week, here’s a prophetic Scripture and a poem for you to read and contemplate.

“Ask for the old paths, where is the good way, and walk therein.”

Jeremiah 6:16

What does that mean to you?

Learn Faith and Works are Bonded

item.title: Parsha Points - Va Yeitzei (“He went out”)
item.description: Transformation. Will you pay the price?
item.content:encoded:
Audio edition of Parsha Points - Va Yeitzei (“He went out”) on Contender's Voice. For more, visit contendersvoice.com.

Book of Genesis

Parsha VaYeitzei (“He went out”)

Transformation. Will you pay the price?

Part 1

Doers are the most blessed.

Do you know, dear reader, why you have been chosen to follow Messiah Yeshua? If you are unsure I will gladly inform you. Believers are directed to perform a profound, life-changing duty! It is to become “...doers of the Word and not hearers only...” (James 1:22-24). And furthermore, to keep on enduring and growing as “doers of the Word of God.” The ardent sheep who follow Yeshua the good Shepherd without compromise and obey His precepts and commands are quite different from many of the worldly Church goers of this age. Of His set-apart, sanctified followers the King of Glory says: “Yea, rather blessed are they that hear the word of God and keep it” (Luke 11:28 KJV). Friend, there is no discipleship apart from following the ways and obeying words of the Messiah. So saint, you can remain as you are, or set your course for uncompromised discipleship and undergo a lifetime of transformation.

Cherry picking

Swarms of casual Bible readers have maintained that the Gospel has set aside the instructions [laws] of the Torah and that believers are therefore free from any obligation to obey it. Such was the doctrine of the Nicolatians which was so severely rebuked by Messiah Yeshua. [See Revelation 2:15]. They mistakenly supposed that the Messiah had delivered them from strict adherence to the Law of Moses and given them the Spirit to follow instead. Thus, the leading of (1) the Spirit was their foremost rule of life instead of (2) the written Law of God. Obedience is not legalism. Rather it is an unabashed, bold demonstration of biblical faith and pure worship.

False Doctrine

Note: The Law and the Spirit actually exist in conformity! They are two sides of the same shekel, you could say. In any case, the faulty Nicolatians’ doctrine represents Yeshua and the Holy Spirit as having taken up arms openly against the government of the Kingdom of God. Point: The liberty of the Gospel does not consist of being free from doing what Yahweh’s Law requires. Force is not the issue. Consider: Rather, a “born again” person’s inner being, through faith in Yeshua as Savior, becomes--in an instant, miraculously transformed with a new heart (spirit), an enlightened mind, and a desire given by the Spirit to obey all known, pertinent and doable holy words of Yahweh. Such faithful compliance becomes a pleasure, renews the mind, and over time conspicuously draws the compliant believer toward Christlikeness. Reader, adhering to divine instructions is never a legalistic burden and places no faith follower of Yeshua under the law.

A sobering forecast.

“Not everyone who says to me, Lord, Lord” will enter the kingdom of heaven, but he who does the will of My Father who is in heaven will enter” (Matthew 7:21). Parsha point: Welcome the work of the Holy Spirit, commit to daily prayer, study the Word of God, and present your body as a living sacrifice. And you will be transformed by the renewal of our minds through obedience to His sacred truth. Make yourself ready.

Parsha VaYeitzei (“He went out”)

References: Genesis 28:10-32:2; Hosea 12:12-14:9; John 1:43-51.

He went out to Haran as Jacob the deceiver. He came back to Beersheba as Israel. Is your “Faith Journey”radically transforming you, dear reader?

A Brief Survey

VaYeitzei (“And he went out”) is the first of the last six parshas in Genesis, and all of them feature Jacob prominently. He is the third and the last of the patriarchs. In broad strokes, the parsha encompasses (1) Jacob’s departure from Beersheba and his family, (2) his first night away and his re-affirming dream, (3) his arrival in Haran and serving Laban, (4) obtaining wives and children, (5) the events occuring during his return to Beersheba, (6) the covenant with Laban, and (7) the accompaniment of two groups of

Angelic escorts as Jacob returns home, wrestling with the LORD, and reconciliation with Esau.

Read the whole parsha. There’s much more!

In our Genesis Manual we also teach about the Holy Spirit’s ministry. Elijah--the runaway prophet is remembered, the visions from the “hideout” cave and their meaning aree shared, and the “still small voice” we all need to hear. Consider: If you enroll in our Torah and Glory School in 2027, we will send you the 347 page manual, the first step in our five manual year-long, college level Torah Commentary course. Information will be released soon.

Jacob journeyed. A look at Bethel.

It is written: “Jacob went out from Beersheba, and went toward Haran. And he lighted upon a certain palace, and tarried there all night…and lay down…and he dreamed…” (see Genesis 28:10-12). This dream was a life-changing, prophetic event and a powerful affirmation of Jacob’s destiny! During his first night the lonely traveler slept and had a divine visitation, and an affirmation of the covenant Yahweh made with Abraham and Isaac: “Your descendants will become like the dust of the earth, and you will spread out [break forth like a flood especially after the House of Israel is divided and dispersed to the nations] ...and in you shall all the families of the earth be blessed. And behold, I am with you” (Genesis 28:14-15). This affirmation and the special superintendence and care Jacob experienced during his time away from home would carry him and his family all the way into Egypt where his family would grow into the nation–Israel. And that nation would in time receive the advent of the divine Son of Elohim, the Messiah of Judah and the royal House of David.

All New Covenant, Spirit-born believers in the Messiah are chosen.

Point: In the Torah, the Israelites are referred to as Benei Yesrael, which means “the descendants of Israel.” Israel became Jacob’s other, divinely given name. Nevertheless, Jacob’s children–twelve sons and one daughter--were not perfect people. Still, they were raised and educated in the knowledge of El Shaddai. Among their ranks there were no departures among them to idols or false gods. For this reason Jacob [Israel] is known as the eponymous father of the Israelite people. From there he traveled to Haran. Yahweh’s power and position are sometimes not noticed by people.

Desire the Holy Spirit to be your Tutor

To affirm the superintendence and special care of Yahweh over His chosen people, the Elohim of Abraham and Isaac went on to (1) proclaim His personal name, YHWH, and (2) affirm to the sleeper that he was the heir to the covenant with Jacob’s fathers, and to (3) renew to Jacob the promises he had made earlier with him. See verses 13-15. Point: Jacob was favored and his journey holds encouragement for you and me. Note: Take a break from Sunday sermons to pray and study with the Holy Spirit looking over your shoulder. Elohim’s Spirit will teach you, and open Scripture for you to understand. You are chosen for service also.

Tamid Kadima-Always Forward. Hutch Church, Part 2 is next. You are in for a surprise. Let’s meet there.

item.title: Parsha Points: Toldot (“Generations”) Part 2
item.description: Whose Path are YOU on?
item.content:encoded:
Audio edition of Parsha Points: Toldot (“Generations”) Part 2 on Contender's Voice. For more, visit contendersvoice.com.

Book of Genesis

Toldot (“Generations”) Part 2

WHOSE PATH ARE YOU ON?

A Central Truth: Jacob’s journey to Padan-aram, undertaken in obedience to his parents wishes, is an example of transformation and providential favor that is experienced when someone follows the divine directives of the Almighty or even the wise instructions of godly parents. Hence, Jacob journeyed on a prophetic pathway that produced life changing, positive characteristics from which he and many others benefited during his lifetime. Consider: Should not the journeys we western saints undertake during our stay on earth be blessed in a similar way? Yes! And they will be if our pathways and motives are in accordance with Yahweh’s prophetic Word. As it is written: “And He will make your paths straight” (Proverbs 3:6).

This Parsha teaches us, blessed reader, that our “life journey” can be similar to that of Jacob embarked upon. His journey was:

  1. A Pathway of Purpose.

Jacob, the elect of Yahweh, had been singled out as Abraham’s covenant heir. Consequently, with the assistance of his discerning mother Rebecca, he received the blessing of his beguiled father, Isaac, who spoke affirming promises of purpose over him: “Therefore God give you the dew of heaven, the fatness of the earth, and plenty of corn and wine; let people serve you…” (See 27:28-29). Isaac spoke later over Esua, the worldly brother. However, the wording was entirely opposite of that spoken over Jacob. The Hebrew translation reads, ”Behold, your dwelling shall be away from the fatness of the earth and away from the dew of heaven.” Point: The story of Esua reminds us that we all have to face the unfortunate consequences of sinful and reckless choices. See Samual 12:7-14 for confirmation. But also learn this: Repentance is the means for entering and progressing ons God’s pathway and fulfilling His prophetic purposes. Furthermore, the key to uncompromised repentance is obedience to all known, relevant, and doable sacred truth; i.e., His holy instruction. This is how the great commandments of Deuteronomy 6:4-8 are fulfilled.

  1. A Pathway of Duty

A good son obeys his father and mother. As it is written: He “...hears the instruction of his father and forsakes not the law of his mother” (Proverbs 1:8). Obedience to Yahweh’s instructions welcomes His wisdom. Moreover, keeping His commandments is the whole duty of man. Point: Turn toward His precepts, not away from them.

  1. A Pathway of Promise

Isaac charged Jacob to arise and go to Padan-aram and there to find and take a wife. Isaac had become aware of the ascendency of his younger son and spoke a second prophetic blessing upon him–”May He also give you the blessing of Abraham, to you and your descendants, that you may possess the land of your sojourning, which God gave Abraham” (28:4).

  1. A Pathway of Hope

When Jacob left his parents in Beersheba he took with him on his long journey great and precious promises. Point: Modern believers also have promises. Many of them, as revealed in the Scriptures--enlighten, direct and elevate us on our pathway through life.

Jacob was, no doubt, downcast and dispirited when he bid goodbye to his mother and father, and left home. Remember, he was a man of the tent, not of the outdoors, and was accustomed to the constant company, instructions, pampering and protection of his parents.

  1. A Pathway of Blessing.

Jacob received two powerful prophetic benedictions pronounced over him, instilling direction and confidence for his arduous journey. It is written: “...for blessed are they that keep my ways’ (Proverbs 8:32).

Hope in the Lord and renew your strength.

Nevertheless, Jacob was sustained by the hope of the prophetic benedictions and the cheerful prospect of an affectionate wife and children as implied in the promise. With hope, Jacob went forward, one step at a time. Learn: Today’s saints should also live with biblical hope sustaining them! It is written: “...lay hold upon the hope [eternal life, abundant life, covenant promises] set before us: which hope we have as an anchor of the soul, both sure and steadfast…” (Heb 6:18-19). Keep in mind: Hope does not calm or remove the storms of tribulation, rather hope holds fast the vessel in the storm.

This pertains directly to you, my attentive friend.

Why did Jacob prevail in history? Well, the person, family, or nation whose standards

are seated upon scriptural foundations of truth are thereby leavened with divine wisdom,

favor, spiritual enlightenment, and providential oversight. Such people will appreciate and adhere to their blessed prophetic destiny–as declared by the Word of God and the Spirit of Truth, and rise above and overcome the corruption of worldly evils. Consider: The person who is bonded to Yahweh and honors His Words is easily distinguished from the person who does not. In parsha Toldot we see two men from the same home with two motivations, two prophecies, two paths, and two remarkably different destinies.

The Bride makes herself ready.

The importance of discerning and understanding what the Scriptures declares to us,

the Betrothed of Messiah, personally--cannot be overstated. Recognize Ecclesia’s end times destiny and prepare for your role, as you are led to perceive it. His word of prophecy enables us to prepare and position ourselves in the purpose, power, and place of the flow of Yahweh’s restorative strength and vision. This will inspire you to participate in a meaningful way in the New Covenant Royal Priesthood that is subject to Yeshua our High Priest. With that is mind, be watchful and pray daily for apostolic level discipleship to be restored to the stumbling, westernized Ecclesia. See Isaiah 46:9-10

Effort is required of disciples.

By observing Jacob we have seen what connects spiritual vitality to the believer hence and amplifies meaning to our lives. It is understanding and incorporating, by faith, YHWH’s personally applicable prophetic word of Scripture into our personal existence. Learn:”Take heed, watch and pray” (Mark 13:33) as did Isaac and Rebecca. Be diligent. Strive to become compliant to biblical authority–as did Jacob. Return to the pure apostolic faith. Finally, as Yeshua’s disciple – pray for him to be baptized with the Holy Spirit. He will do it.

Steerage class.

Humility is the channel of power!

We learn from the lives and deaths of Abraham and Sarah that the true estimate

of a servant’s life and influence are found in his/her relationship to Yahweh and His sacred Word. Nonetheless, a servant is a “minister,” not a “lord.” The word “minister” once referred to someone being an “under-rower” on a large boat, a common sailor who manned an oar and was usually found among the lower class of workers. Ministers then were about equal to “steerage” class people who slept in the dank, lower level of the boat’s hull that was below the waterline. Point: We disciples of Yeshua would do well to remember we are summoned to be humble servants of the Messiah, under-rowers who have no authority or power of our own other than what we receive from Him. Amen.

He will guide you into all truth.

We have discovered that which connects true prosperity and meaning to life. It is understanding and incorporating Yahweh’s inspired, prophetic words into one existence. Remember Jacob! The person who continually disdains and scorns His prophetic opportunity revealed in Scripture, or does not fully conform to it, will miss his earthly destiny and forgo the highest blessing once reserved. Remember Esau. And finally, here’s a challenge for you, dear reader: Juxtapose your pathway with Jacob’s. Then line up your pathway with Esau’s. To which one are you currently closest. Recall what has been written for you. Search me, Father. May your Spirit reveal to me the true spiritual disposition of my heart…and lead me in the everlasting way. Psalm 139:23.

Calibrate your doctrines.

Here’s your promise: “Give thanks to the God of heaven. His love [for you] endures forever” (Psalm 136:26). He will impart wisdom, vision, and spiritual vitality as He accompanies you during your “life journey” on the narrow road, the same as He did with Jacob. Therefore, keep your confidence in Him and be glad. You will succeed in fulfilling your call as an overcomer. And start praying daily. It maintains close fellowship

Tamid Kadima-Always Forward. Hutch Church. Shalom. Notice: Parsha Vayeitzei (“And he went out”) is next. Jacob is featured prominently. He is the last of the patriarchs. In the Torah the Israelites are referred to as Benei Yisrael, which means “the descendants of Israel”. Have a blessed week.

item.title: Contenders Voice Weekly Parsha Points Toldot (“History“ or “Generations”)
item.description: Equipping Disciples of Messiah Yeshua
item.content:encoded:
Audio edition of Contenders Voice Weekly Parsha Points Toldot (“History“ or “Generations”) on Contender's Voice. For more, visit contendersvoice.com.

Part 1

It should begin with family.

Preview: Parsha Toldot progresses from focusing on the pilgrimage of Abraham and Sarah to highlighting the expansion of their growing family with whom He covenanted. As it is written: “And I will make you a great nation” (Genesis 12:2). Thus, our brief presentation of Elohim’s chosen family picks up with Isaac when he was forty years old. After the death of Abraham, Isaac and Rebecca continued the saga of redemption. Ishmael had no significant personal role in the ongoing story of the patriarchs or the history of Israel itself. Yet his name means “God hears.” That’s significant. Point: It proclaims perpetually that the Almighty is essentially a Hearer of prayer, and is not far from them that cry out to Him. Even those scattered, who are far off and in despair, He will hear. When the lad was laid beneath the shrub in the wilderness, YHWH heard his cry. Beresheit 21:17. Nevertheless, the redemption story went forth with Isaac. And it continues with you, dear reader.

A blessed Domicile

Toldot means “generations” or “offspring.” The word pertains to that which a person generates or produces–actually, a legacy. The Toldot of Isaac (Yitzchak) and Rebecca (Rivka) were Esau (Esav) and Jacob (Yaakov). The parsha includes their births and the event of Isaac’s blessing, sibling hostility, and Jacob going to Haran to find a wife among his people. Point: The family unit is the place where discipleship training begins. In other words, a sanctified home is where the Messiah’s people prepare a new generation, or toldot, of godly saints.

Equipped to become Deputies.

Purpose: We present two basic points today: First, to inform Messiah Yeshua’s saints that all of His followers are appointed and accountable to fulfill their responsibility of establishing a morally and spiritually prosperous toldot. Again, that refers to a generation or one’s offspring. In any case, it is our first order of business. Secondly, the intention of this post is to inform Messiah’s followers that they have been redeemed and equipped to be His vice-regents on earth; i.e., deputies acting in the place of a ruler. In our case, that ruler would be King Yeshua with the proclamation of His victorious Gospel--by word and by lifestyle.

You are needed as a Doer.

Are you building a legacy of children or disciples who actually believe the Gospel and

observe the Redeemer’s commands, and do not remain stalled on conversion decisions and casual faith? 1. If so, turn around and start marching to His cadence today! 2. Here is your foundation: Deuteronomy 6:4-8, John 3:16-36, and Matthew 28:18-20. 3. Conform to His instructions! Warning: The term “reject” found in John 3:36 is translated from the Greek word apeitheo. It means to “disobey“ or “not be subject to.” Thus, to reject or disregard the Son’s words is tantamount to blatant unbelief. Learn to be a “doer of the Word” and also raise up “doers” yourself. Dilly dally no longer. Prepare yourself as ardent believers are now doing to become the Bride that our coming King expects. Friend, this is the Almighty’s only path to the effectual, enlightening transformation of your soul, character, worldview, and temperament. Challenge: Think “apostolic discipleship.” There’s no other. You will fInd its core in Romans 1 and 16. Text when you discover it. It’s this...or remain as you are now. You decide.

Love His Words and Ways.

“A pupil [disciple] is not above his teacher; but everyone, after he has been [fully equipped] trained, will become like his teacher” (Luke 6:40). A true disciple’s desire is to become like the master (teacher) to whom he has joined himself. It is YHWH’s will that believers be so--that is, that they become conformed to the image of His eternal Son, Yeshua. “For those whom he foreknew, He also predestined to become conformed to the image [spiritual likeness, moral character] of His Son…” (Romans 8:29). Charge: This is your duty and fortune, friend.

Parsha Toldot (“Family”)

Genesis 25:19-28:9; Joshua 1:7-15; Malachi 1:1-2:7; Matthew 1:1-17; Romans 9:6-16; Hebrews 12:14-17.

An ancient pathway.

There are numerous stories intersecting that comprise parsha Toldot. As you know, these include, for instance--the heartfelt praying of Isaac and Rebecca, the birth Esau and Jacob, the birthright issue, well digging, Isaac blessing Jacob, and Jacob’s flight to Laban. However, at this time we will benefit most from focusing upon the road of faith that Jacob followed and what it teaches us who also tread on prophetic roads and ancient paths today.

Four powerful assets for Believers. Lay hold of them.

Dear reader, parsha Toldot is introducing us to a new era in the history of Israel. The focus is shifting from the faith and character development of individuals, i.e., Abraham and Isaac, to the unfolding purposes and design of the Almighty for the covenant family. Always observable in the working of YHWH’s covenant are (1) divine interposition [YHWH intervening for His people by placing Himself between them and their enemies], (2) supernatural assistance for human frailty and weakness, (3) the reliable word of prophecy, and (4) the steady leadership of the Holy Spirit, your Counselor and Comforter. Listen for His words as you pray and study.

Birthright for Pottage.

“And Jacob said [to Esau], Sell me this day thy birthright” (25:31). With regard to Esau, he apparently acted like a pious son before his father, but was a carnal man who in truth had little regard for spiritual heirship. So he sold his firstborn birthright to Jacob. Saying “...what profit shall this birthright do to me.” Discernment: Esua’s reckless, foolish words revealed his ignorance and disinterest for sacred spiritual blessings, and exposed his (a) lack of prophetic foresight and (b) narrowness of vision for a blessed future. Jacob, on the other hand, secured the promise: “Swear to me this day…” And Esua agreed, clearly and verbally. Point: Words are important and will shape our future. So Jacob got the birthright and Esau got the pottage. Esua is a type of the person who is bonded to the dark world and rejects the Gospel, but accepts the carnal fragments of the devil’s kingdom in exchange. Sad.

Application

Today, believers are the Toldot of Yahweh. This relationship phenomenon occurs through one’s faith in Messiah Yeshua and the miraculous spiritual birth wrought by the Spirit of Elohim, our Creator. He is the power of our discipleship. As you know, the Holy Spirit came with power on the day of Pentecost and united 120 believers [disciples] of Yeshua where they were praying. They began to speak in tongues and went out into the streets where people from every part of the Roman Empire heard the gospel in their own language. Through the power of the Holy Spirit 3000 of them came to faith in the Messiah that day. And the same Spirit brought them into unity with other believers” [4B] Exhortation: Pray to be baptized with the Holy Spirit. Just do it! Keep asking. (Mt. 7:7-11). Persevere. You will get blessed as promised.

The blessed Gift

Point: Know that the Holy Spirit brings power and unity to the disciples. He exalts and magnifies the Messiah. He empowers us, the saints, to know Yeshua without reserve, and believe Him, obey Him, follow Him, bear witness of Him, and grow in His likeness as you become transformed. Learn: This is sanctification, the separation of a saint/disciple from the world and consecration to Yahweh and His Son. It is a life-long process that only the Holy Spirit can accomplish. For this reason the Savior promised, “Ye shall receive power [for all this wonderful work] after that the Holy Spirit has come upon you” (Acts 1:8). The promise is written for us today as well. The power we are promised and that we all need for the most effectual ministry has been placed into us; “...the Spirit of truth…He abides with you and shall be in you” (John 14:17). Amazing. Therefore understand: Receiving the Holy Spirit is not an option, it is a privilege and a duty.

Toldot Part 2 is next. Meet me there. We will follow Jacob as he proceeds on his journey and also continue to discuss the importance of the Holy Spirit in the life and ministry of today’s modern Toldot.

Tamid Kadima--Always Forward. Hutch Church. Shalom.

item.title: Contenders Voice Weekly Parsha Points
item.description: Book of Genesis Parsha Chayei Sarah (“Life of Sarah”) - Part 2
item.content:encoded:
Audio edition of Contenders Voice Weekly Parsha Points on Contender's Voice. For more, visit contendersvoice.com.

Prepare for Eternity.

Modern Biblical ministries should turn around and start preaching the complete, holy Word of God instead of seeking to entertain, be inclusive, and avoid unpopular doctrines as many do today. Point: Motivational talks and sermons about overcoming life’s everpresent obstacles and carnal temptations may leave people feeling encouraged temporarily, but encouragement without biblical backup and scriptural faith cannot replace the systematic teaching of God’s Word. [1]

Follow wisdom.

Good results come by honoring heavenly instructions. It is written: “And Abraham was old…and said to the eldest servant of his house [Eliezer] that ruled over all he had…I will make thee swear by the Lord…go unto my country, and to my kindred, and take a wife for my son Isaac” (24:1-4). The legacy of Sarah had to be perpetuated, and the promised seed must be propagated. Such were the deep concerns of Abraham. He knew he had to find a suitable wife for Isaac. But the patriarch would not send off his only “son of promise” alone into the idolatrous world of the Chaldeans to find himself a wife. It is the Word of Yahweh that gives direction and inspires faith, hope, and love!

A pearl in the field.

Abraham remembered (a) the idolatry in Chaldea and (b) the outcome of his nephew Lot, who had strayed from listening to sound wisdom and flirted with the corruption of Sodom. The sacred inheritance would be endangered by exposing Isaac to the temptation of remaining in the “old country” in case his new wife refused to return with him. So Abraham enlisted his trusted servant Eliezer to find and fetch an appropriate wife from the patriarch’s own people and bring her to Canaan.

A servant must be found faithful.

Eliezer pledged his fidelity and was guided by the Holy Spirit. His journey was successful and blessed. He arrived at Nahor’s home in Haran, and prayed for God to bless his master Abraham, not himself. He quickly found Rebecca, recognized her grace and kindness, and bowed and worshiped the Almighty. Eliezer went forward to meet Rebecca and her congenial family. He quickly made all necessary arrangements and departed to Canaan, as it is written: “...the servant took Rebecca and went his way. And Isaac came…And Rebecca lifted up her eyes, and when she saw Isaac, she lighted off the camel…and Isaac brought her into the tent of Sarah, his mother, and took Rebecca, and she became his wife” (24:62-77). Consider what is written: “Surely LORD, you will bless the righteous; you will surround them with your favor as with a shield” (Psalm 5:2).

Learn: YHWH is as willing to answer our prayers as he was with Eliezer, the servant of Abraham. Afterall, He confirms this for today’s saints: “In everything give thanks: for this is the will of Elohim in Messiah Yeshua concerning you” (1 Thessalonica 5:18).

Abraham, in the course of time, took a second wife [or concubine]. Her name is given as Keturah, and she was probably a servant to the family. In any case, Abraham’s vitality and reproductive powers, which were rejuvenated for the conception of Isaac, apparently continued undiminished. Learn: “For the gifts and callings of God are without repentance [irrevocable]” (Romans 11:29). He and Keturah had six sons! Still, Abraham’s son with Sarah was constituted as his only “heir of promise” in compliance with the counsel of Yahweh.

The patriarch lived to a good old age and his end was peaceful. “...the days of the years of Abraham’s life...one hundred threescore and fifteen years [175 years]…” (25:7-90). He was buried in the Promised Land, in his own tomb, next to the remains of Sarah in the cave of Machpelah.

Although Abraham had multiple descendants for which he provided, he carefully distinguished Isaac as the true heir of the promised blessing of the covenant--and in the end “...gave all he had unto Isaac” (25:5).. Learn: The lessons we have presented are gleaned from this parsha but do not apply to the Hebrews only, they pertain to modern believers of the New Covenant who are supernaturally born of the Spirit of God through faith only in Yeshua.

Understand who you are!

“If you belong to Christ, then you are Abraham’s seed [descendants, and heirs according to the promise” (Galatians 3:29). Point: Scripture does add the word “spiritual” before seed or “zera”--sperm. The noun is purely physical. The word is regularly used as a collective in the singular (never plural). This is an important aspect of the promise doctrine, for Hebrew never uses the plural of this root to refer to posterity, or offspring. Thus the word is deliberately flexible enough to denote either one person (Messiah) who epitomizes the whole group, or the many persons in that entire lineage of natural-spiritual descendents”.

Holiness is transformative.

“Salvation is a revelation of who you are, and were, despite the fact that you did not know it. The fact that you belong to Yeshua then becomes the truth and the doorway into the revelation that you are Abraham’s seed [Galatians 3:29] both spiritually and physically” by a miraculous spiritual birth and heavenly decree. [Restoration Scriptures; Commentary; p. 969 Third Edition; Your Arms to Israel Publishing.]

Keep in mind: God is good, gracious, and has a heart of loving kindness toward you.

Therefore blessed readers, go forward into the realms of eternity and come to know Him in a deeper, more profound, life-changing way. Amen [2]

Tamid Kadima-Always Forward. Hutch Church; Comment: hutchchurch@gmail.com Shalom.

Next

Parsha Toldot (“History”) is next. Learn of YHWH’s plan for growing the generations of Abraham and Sarah with whom He covenanted. In fact, Yahweh has plans for the spiritual development and service of your generations also. He could be knocking on your door right now! Open it! Enter your prayer closet and listen for Him to speak to your heart as you pray and read the Holy Word of God. Believe–He wants to engage! Amen.

  1. PNW. 2. Message of the Month edited. K.S.

item.title: Contenders Weekly Parsha Points
item.description: Purpose: To glean Torah insights for strengthening and equipping the endtime Ecclesia.
item.content:encoded:
Audio edition of Contenders Weekly Parsha Points on Contender's Voice. For more, visit contendersvoice.com.

Book of Genesis

Parsha Chayei Sarah (“Life of Sarah”)

Our Goal: Make prophetic disciples who will work to restore Torah and Spirit centered truth to the westernized spiritual Body of Messiah Yeshua.

Consider: Blessed friend, what is your purpose in life? Upon what foundation are you building your legacy? See Matthew 7:24-27. Can you recall that important Scripture? What’s more, have you been baptised in the Holy Spirit? If not, you remain inadequately equipped to contend with the spiritual warfare that’s intensifying throughout the nation.

Part 1

Friend, the Almighty has already called you to rise above simple conversion and become an ardent disciple of Messiah Yeshua. I assume you have responded as did John and James when they were summoned by Yeshua, who said, “Follow Me” to them and they obeyed without hesitation. In fact, it is recorded that he gave that command twenty-one times in the Bible. Therefore, you have been chosen also. Therefore, you should…”know full well that the road leading to the Promised Land ‘flowing with milk and honey’ of necessity also runs by way of mount Sinai, flowing with ‘thou shalts’ and ‘thou shalt nots.’” [1B]

Hence reader, earnestly consider the challenge you face and prepare yourself for committing to apostolic discipleship. It is a blessed and sanctified lifestyle with expectations. John the apostle clearly avered: ”The one who keeps His commandments abides in Him, and He in him” (1 John 5:5:24) It speaks of apostolic faith. So, if you have not yet committed yourself, are you prepared to reconsider and embrace real discipleship and the profound transformation that accompanies it? Selah.

Central Truth: There are those today who want “liberation” from having to honor the Law [instructions; standards] of the Almighty–which actually paves the way of spiritual liberty. Instead they prefer carnal license and an undemanding worldly faith. Such lukewarm believers are not disciples at all, but remain as regular westernized Christians. Point. The Kingdom of God and its Sovereign, Messiah Yeshua, cannot be separated from their standards. Thus, to live in the spiritual Kingdom now is to live by His teaching now. It is written: “By this we know that we have come to know Him, if we keep His commandments’”(1 John 2).

Understand: Many believers, it seems, become easily fascinated by worldly interests and religious fantasies. However, the one who is truly led by the Holy Spirit will end up at the Torah, the instructions provided by God which enable His covenant people to live holy, contented, and prosperous lives. Sarah’s life demonstrates the value of faithfulness . Let’s read about her.

Parsha Chayei Sarah (“Life of Sarah”)

References: Genesis 23:1-25:18; 1 Kings 1:1-31; Matthew 8:19-22; Luke 9:57-62.

“And Sarah was a hundred and seven and twenty years old: these were the years of Sarah’s life. Sarah died in Kiriath-arba which is in Hebron in the land of Canaan.” (B’resheit 23:1-2).

A woman of character.

Sarah, the beloved and faithful wife of Abraham, was the mother of the promised seed, Isaac, and is considered today as the “faith mother” of all believers. When she died she was 127 years old; Isaac was thirty-seven at that time. She was the only woman whose age is mentioned in Scriptures. One rabbinic writer said her age revealed that she had (1) the exuberance of a seven year old, (2) the beauty of a twenty year old, (3) the wisdom of a one hundred year old.

In any case she was a woman of faith, even as her husband was a man of faith. It is written of her: “By faith also Sarah herself received strength to conceive seed, even when she was past age…” (Hebrews 11:11). She died in Canaan, YHWH’s land and her inheritance. Learn: We observe from the Matriarch’s life the attributes we should all develop! They include loyalty to a commitment, the balance between strength and compassion, devotion to family, marriage loyalty, and faith in the Word of YHWH-Hoshe’ah–”the LORD who saves.”

Only the right woman

Abraham had lived as a wanderer and pilgrim in Canaan, but after the death of Sarah he actually purchased land for a sepulcher. The loyal friend of El Shaddai, which is a title meaning God Almighty, desired to acquire a proper burial site–a sepulcher befitting the greatness of his wife. He found such a site at the Cave of Machpellah, which means “double,” or having two chambers–suggesting that couples would be entombed there. Anyway, Abraham paid an exorbitant price for the property. It was a practical and necessary acquisition but also an act of faith in the promise of Elohim, Genesis 12:1-3; 15:17-18.

Abraham paid silver for the cave and the field became a pledge for the whole land, and...“the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not [yet] seen.” One day his seed would possess and own it. After the burial of Sarah, Abraham turned his attention to finding a wife befitting the heir to the holy promise, his son Isaac. The patriarch sent his faithful servant Eliezer to fetch an appropriate wife from Abraham’s own people, among whom there was still knowledge of the one true Elohim, and bring her back to Canaan and his son Isaac.

Under no condition would Isaac be permitted to marry a daughter of the Canaanites. Eliezer carried a heavy responsibility and prayed fervently during his journey, that he would be successful in fulfilling his charge. Yahweh guided him and Abraham’s trusted servant returned to Canaan with a woman named Rebecca from Abraham’s people. Learn:

A representation of selflessness.

Eliezer was a man of true faith that was based upon the Word of God and learned from Abraham, his master, and probably Shem as well. Such tutoring gave him a more clear spiritual insight than do (a) human common sense or (b) reasoning alone. Point: May our steps in life be guided by the Holy Spirit as was the mind of Abraham and the heart of his trusted chief servant, Eliezer, the man of prayer and faith.

Note: In fact, Eliezer is a type, or a representation, of the Holy Spirit Whom the Father has sent to gather into His Kingdom the scattered remnant of the House of Israel, and restore and return them to His kingdom House and its standards. This would be the Bride of Messiah Yeshua. Rebecca is a typ[e of the Bride.

The Spirit of Elohim is currently restoring many believers who are in covenant with Yeshua through faith to the knowledge of their faith’s Hebraic origins, Israelite identity, and their heritage of the Torah and the fullness of the Holy Spirit. Point: “In every thing give thanks; for this is the will of Elohim in Messiah Yeshua concerning you” (1 Thess. 5:18). He is as eager to hear and answer your prayers as He was to answer those of Eliezer. Remember, by sincere prayer even seemingly insurmountable difficulties can be overcome. Here’s your Word: “The Lord is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble; and he knoweth [takes care of] them that trust in Him” (Nahum 1:7). KJV

Part 2 of Chayei Sarah is next. It features Abraham, his second wife, death, burial, and relevant life lessons.

Tamid Kadima–Always Forward. Hutch Church. Shalom.

item.title: He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit
item.description: Matthew 3:11. - Yeshua is your Baptizer
item.content:encoded:
Audio edition of He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit on Contender's Voice. For more, visit contendersvoice.com.

“Now the Lord said to Abraham, Go fourth, so Abraham went forth…” Gen 12:1.

Our Elohim speaks to, or openly communicates with, common saints like you and me--audibly at times, Spirit to spirit, Mind to mind, Heart to heart, and by the Holy Spirit through the Word. 1 Cor. 12. He says, “I will guide you in the way of wisdom and lead you in straight paths” (Prov. 4:11). Yes, He cares and will (a) renew your vision, (b) give fresh hope, (c) inspire faith, (d) bestow personal instructions, (e) impart understanding and wisdom, and (f) activate ministry gifts for service. So, are you eager to consciously receive His personal input? Learn: All born-again believers are summoned and supernaturally positioned to pass through spiritual stages, or phases, in developing a Scripturally based mindset and gaining experience with the Holy Spirit. Thus, we need to believe and pay attention to the Gospels and the Book of Acts which showcase the miraculous. The point: Your faith journey is (or should be) an upward progression of experience in Spirit and Truth leading toward a more sublime fellowship with your good Shepherd Yeshua, an attraction to sanctification, and the miraculous transformation of your soul.

“He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit” (Mt. 3:11).

“For it is by grace you have been saved through faith, and it is the gift of God, not of works, so that no one can boast” (Ephesians 2:8). Faith in Messiah Yeshua and the spiritual birth spoken of in John 3:16 are the only means by which anyone can have a genuine personal relationship with almighty God. John 3:16. Subsequent to the New Birth however, there is a very important experience believers need and can receive today. Following His resurrection, these are the assuring words Yeshua spoke to His followers: ”You shall receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you...” (Acts 1:8) In Acts our Messiah speaks concerning the baptism in the Holy Spirit which is accompanied by the evidence of the recipients speaking in other tongues, a Spirit inspired personal prayer language. [Mt. 3:11; Acts 1:8; 2:1-4; 10:46; 19:6;1 Cor. 12:10-30; 145:39]. Furthermore, the baptism in the Holy Spirit can be likened to an immersion in water, so to speak. It is the complete filling and over-flowing of the believing saint in the presence and power of the Spirit of Elohim. Speaking in tongues, a personal supernatural prayer language, is an integral part confirming the blessing. Point: Don’t be turned aside, as many have been, by unbelieving saints or contrary denominational doctrines. Tongues are the supernatural language of the Spirit. Unfortunately people today deride, insult, or simply dismiss this holy promise and especially its initial evidence. Such nay-saying is unprofitable and forms a barrier restricting the spiritual blessing from being experienced by many spiritually malnourished, hungry believers. This is a colossal mistake and a grievance perpetuated by (1) fundamental Christian secessionists, (2) false teaching of Scripture, (3) the dis-interest of Torah-focused ministries, and (4) the orthodoxy of westernized Chrisitanity, for example. Point: Discrediting personal “tongues” as the initial evidence of the baptism in the Holy Spirit for modern believers, and insisting instead that speaking native languages or dialects which occurred on Pentecost is the only evidence--is not accurate. Such notions run against the weight of Scripture and personal biblical evidence. This is the teaching of Contenders voice.

Where’s the Beef?

Consider: Widespread denominational tunnel vision sustains the prejudicial view that restricts the Spirit’s full ministry. Wouldn’t we, the sheep of Yeshua, benefit from listening less to what comes from a pulpit and resort instead to systematic Bible study and listening more to the Spirit of Truth. Modern religious error keeps the western Body of Messiah from restoring whole truth and experiencing and living in a greater measure of Yahweh’s glory, miraculous power, and far-sighted prophetic vision. What’s more, the entrenched unbelief holds much of the nation’s institutional Ecclesia spiritually vitiated, or weakened. It removes from the preaching of Torah-based truth the demonstration of signs, wonders, and supernatural ministry gifts of the Spirit. In other words, rejecting the full, beneficial ministry of the Holy Spirit while preaching God’s Word and serving His people in Church is like going to a restaurant and ordering a hamburger that contains all the pretty fixings but does not provide the necessary vitality of beef patty! In other words, no beef! Heaven have mercy! The result is a rather incomplete, pickle loaded, veggie sandwich. Point: It’s simple! A disciple (a) should be baptized in the Holy Spirit by the Good Shepherd, Yeshua the Son, (b) receive his/her personal prayer language, and (c) enjoy a fresh, personal spiritual revival! Do you believe it? Then undertake your own prayer campaign and ask to “receive power” that has been promised. Don’t give up! Rather, believe and persist! He will visit you.

Gentiles receive the bap;tism!

Go to Acts 10:44-48 and reconsider the family and friends who were assembled in the house of Cornelius following Pentecost, when Peter came and preached. Point: They were all baptized in the Holy Spirit and experienced the very same life-changing phenomenon that occurred on the day of Pentecost with Yeshua’s early disciples! His baptized followers all spoke in native languages or dialects then so the gathered bystanders and visitors from other areas could understand through the speaking. Learn: But in the house of Cornelious there was, most likely, a different sign confirming the experience which was attested to by Peter himself. Read Acts 10 once more! Speaking separate languages was not a necessity! The family and the guests spoke the same language. It is entirely likely therefore, that the assembled guests, as the Holy Spirit and power came upon them in the house, began praising God enthusiastically and speaking forth their personal, Spirit generated prayer language, as Peter attested. It is written: “...they [Peter and his companions] heard them speak in tongues and magnify God” (Acts 10:34-48).

Receive your own Spirit inspired prayer language.

Let’s wrap this cameo up with a comment upon publicly speaking in tongues--such as we read Acts 2. Again, some ministries interpret the disciples “speaking in tongues” as “speaking in known languages or dialects.” Though the issue stirs up some disputes, I think this is probably true. Is it possible, however, that what the assembled, mixed multitude heard long ago on Pentecost were actually the interpretations of tongues, another Spirit inspired phenomenon that the Scriptures teach must openly follow tongues that are publicly spoken. Note: 1 Corinthians 14:6-17:27. New Covenant Scripture instructs believers that if anyone speaks in “a tongue” publically, it should occur by two or three, and each in turn with someone “interpreting” by the Spirit, what is said in a known language. The interpretation in the known language assures the divine message of public tongues spoken forth will be understood and hence beneficial in the church (public assembly) setting. Review 1 Corinthians 12. Nevertheless, this instruction does not apply to the private use of a Spirit-baptized saint’s inspired personal prayer language; i.e. private tongues. Praying, singing, and simply using your personal spirit-led tongues is a spiritually enriching practice and blessing. Thus, I encourage every reader to seek this baptism. It is powerful for breaking strongholds and elevating the baptized saint’s worship, prayer life, and uplifting, experiential communion with Yeshua, our High Priest.
