item.description: Purpose: To glean Torah insights for nourishing and equipping the endtime Ecclesia.
item.content:encoded:
Audio edition of Contenders Weekly Parsha Points on Contender's Voice. For more, visit contendersvoice.com.

Book of Genesis

Parsha Va Yeira (“He Appeared”)

Part 2

”Blessed are the peacemakers.”

The third faith engagement features Abraham and Isaac, his son of promise. Abraham was not merely a tent dweller, but was a statesman as well. He spent time with Abimelech developing the means of coexisting peacefully in Canaan. Abraham called upon the name of Yahweh El Olam whom he trusted, and peace was established. Consequently a degree of enlightenment was brought to the inhabitants of the region. Afterwards came the great test of Abraham’s faith. It is written. “Now it came about after these things that God tested Abraham, and said to him…Take now your son, your only son, whom your love–Isaac, and go to the land of Moriah, and offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains of which I will tell you” (22:1-2). Consider: Every dedicated follower of Messiah Yeshua will regularly face strenuous trials, strong temptations, rigorous testing, and even tribulations during their lives. Such things are indeed hard to handle, but necessary for exercising faith, developing courage, and learning how to overcome demanding challenges while depending upon the faithfulness of the LORD.

God is no respecter of persons.

Abraham’s unexpected ordeal, his great trial of faith, was announced to him by the Most High. The astonished patriarch was commanded to take his son Isaac and sacrifice him on an altar on Mount Moriah, which is the site of the Temple Mount today. Point: Though severe in form, Abraham’s trial nonetheless declares to us that despite one’s age, favor, and experience, no follower or proclaimer of Yeshua is exempt from trials or is beyond providential testing. Hence be glad for He declares to you now: “For I am the LORD, your God, who takes hold of your right hand and says to you, Do not fear, I will help you” (Isaiah 41:13). Reader, He is preparing you, even now, to be a consistent overcomer!

He is utterly faithful to Provide and Protect.

The patriarch’s trial was a severe test of his faith and relationship with the Almighty. It was overwhelming in its requirement but needful in its design. The vast covenant blessing was conditioned upon the fulfillment of Yahweh’s command by the patriarch, and such would reveal the extent of his heartfelt trust in the pure, unadulterated Word of God. Not until that particular standpoint had been reached in Abraham’s spiritual development was he able to follow through with such a direct order of that nature. When Isaac was born, the son and heir of the promise, there was still the threat that Abraham’s beloved son, and not the sacred Word of God, would be the ground of Abraham’s confidence and joy. But his obedience proved that the commandments and promises of Yahweh were in fact the priorities governing His life. Point: Ultimately, our faith must not rest with circumstances or experiences, but only with the pure Word of Yahweh our Elohim. Amen.

Elohim’s promises are Sure

Abraham, though apprehensive, obeyed without hesitation or pleading. It is written: “...and Abraham built an altar…and bound Isaac his son, and laid him on the altar…and took a knife to slay his son (22:9-10). Here is faith observed in full maturity. Abraham believed, because of the promise of an heir, that though Isaac should be sacrificed [if it actually happened], the Almighty would raise him up from the dead and the Word of Elohim would be yet fulfilled. But it is written: “And the angel of the LORD called out from heaven…lay not your hand upon the lad…(22:11). Abraham staggered not at the promise and therefore gained the victory. See Romans 4:20. The account continues: “...and behold behind him a ram caught in a thicket…and Abraham went and took the ram, and offered him up for a burnt offering instead of his son (verse 13). The father of our faith called the place Yahweh-Jirah which means, “Yahweh will see to it” or “In the mount of the LORD [the place of need] it will be provided [your provision will be seen; your need shall be satisfied].” The ram took Isaac’s place on the altar! Then the reality of dependable great promises of numerous and influential descendents, along with expanded territory, were renewed. Abraham’s course comes to a conclusion and the ultimate fulfillment would be Yeshua. God declares, “because you have done this, and have not withheld your son, your only son, I will surely bless you and multiply your offspring…all the nations of the earth shall be blessed because you have obeyed My voice.” 22:18. Folks, living faith has works.

Three Realities

Consider: 1. Trials will come throughout life, even as we grow older. 2. We overcome evil by faith. This connects us to the promises and power of Elohim. 3. Our security and blessedness are related to our obedience to the truth we have been given…and readiness to advance on into greater light as it is shed on our paths. Great light, when a saint abides within it, always provides for greater fellowship and spiritual intimacy with our beloved Messiah Yeshua. Point: Abraham’s great trial brought great revelation. He was tried so the families of the earth could be blessed. Abraham’s simple faith and calm obedience was reflected in Isaac quietly and peacefully carrying the wood, and thereby he is a type of Yeshua on the cross. The ram is also a typical representation of the Messiah going to the cross. It was on the mount that the provision was seen. Patience is the key to victory. And wisdom is the chief weapon in your spiritual warfare. Think!

Remember!

Abraham’s offering of his son represents Elohim’s wonderful provision for the entire world, a whole burnt offering for the sins of mankind by which humans are redeemed and can experience true joy (“Isaac”, laughter).

Reader’s Application

Eight responsibilities emerge prominently from the narrative and they each apply to you, dear reader! Consider each one thoughtfully because each one of them applies to you. 1. Believe His Word and obey it. Such is not legalism or “coming under the law” as some ignorant people might claim. 2. Practice self-sacrifice. It’s required. 3. Live by faith, not by sight.Trust His promises. 4. Give your best for Yeshua. Aim for 100% 5. Persevere under hardship. You will do well as you walk in the faith, hope, and love footprints of your father of faith, Abraham. 6. Friend, identify yourself thoroughly with Messiah Yeshua, as did Paul who wrote: “But whatever things were gain to me, those things I have counted as loss for the sake of Messiah” (Phil. 3:7). 7. Pray in the Spirit daily. Don’t be slack in fulfilling this responsibility. You are needed to intercede for those going through hardship. And 8. Study the Scriptures day by day and expect to hear from the Spirit of sacred Truth. John 16:13. And be sure that you will be blessed. Start with two or three of these challenges and grow. If you ignore these principles you will not grow beyond just being a convert or Sunday Christian, and never mature as His disciple. These few spiritual standards will come easy, and be satisfying for you very soon. There’s nothing hard about them! You are strong and courageous because His Spirit and Word have taken up residence within you! May your “coming in and going out” be blessed this week. Amen.

Tamid Kadima-Always Forward. Hutch Church. Shalom.

Next week: Contender’s Voice presents Parsha Chayei Sarah (“Life of Sarah”). It includes the death of Sarah and Abraham. Though old age had overtaken them at their respective times the couple had fulfilled their divinely appointed service and accomplished Yahweh’s will for their loves. There are numerous encouraging faith points to glean from this pasha. Meet me there and let’s journey together.

If faith produce no works to see,

That faith is not a living tree.

item.title: Contenders Weekly Parsha Points
item.description: Gleaning Torah insights for nourishing and equipping the end-time Ecclessia
item.content:encoded:
Audio edition of Contenders Weekly Parsha Points on Contender's Voice. For more, visit contendersvoice.com.

Book of Genesis

Parsha Va Yeira (“He Appeared”)

Part 1

In this week’s parsha we are continuing to follow Abraham’s and Sarah’s eventful odyssey into Canaan. Though there is much spiritual significance in this week’s narrative to consider, we will focus on three momentous engagements involving Abraham recorded in this week’s parsha, Va Yeira. These meaningful experiences contributed to developing Abraham’s faith, his righteous character and confidence for victory over obstacles, and deepening his personal fellowship with Yahweh.

Parsha Va Yeira (“He appeared”)

References: Genesis 18:1-22:24; 2 Kings 4:1-37; Luke 17:26-37; Romans 3:19-5:6; Galatianss 4:21-31; Hebrews 6:13-20,

The first faith engagement features Abraham and his heavenly visitors: “Now the Lord appeared to him [Abraham] by the oaks of Mamre, while he was sitting at the tent door in the heat of the day” (B’resheit 18:1). Resting at the door of his tent, and having just eaten, Abraham “looked” [the word implies physical vision] and sees three figures approaching, whom he perceives at first to be just men. However, as they drew close “he saw them” [this implies mental perception, or spiritual discernment] and recognized Yeshua, in preincarnate form, among them. Thus Abraham jumped up and ran toward them, fell on his knees, and then to his face. He lay completely prostrate, we believe, as an act of salutation, reverence, and worship. Upon rising, his words were: “My LORD [Adonai],” a name that is associated with supreme authority.

Yeshua Himself was manifest, along with two angelic escorts, and they had made their way to Abraham’s tent on an un-announced visit. It was noontide when they arrived, and Abraham reverently welcomed them and extended a gracious invitation saying, “...pass not away…a little water…wash…rest yourselves…a piece of bread…comfort your hearts.” The flockmaster knew that by the arrival of the special guests at his doorstep he had a holy responsibility of discharging the most hospitable services. And in this very generous manner he served his visitors, withholding no effort, enjoyment, expense or courtesy. At the end of the meal the divine Being, foremost of the guests, was certainly standing forth as Adonai to Abraham and any other gathered witnesses. Yeshua then made an authoritative announcement: “And lo, Sarah thy wife will have a son.” Upon hearing this, Abraham laughed, (probably) leaped, clapped his hands, and shouted, “Yes, at last!” But Sarah, who was standing by and listening, laughed [or snickered skeptically] as if to say, “Yeah, sure. You’ve got to be kidding me.”

Personal Application

The narrative reveals just two of many ways of laughing. There are also two ways of receiving the Word of God, the sacred promise of the Almighty. One way is by (a) faith, which secures the promise. The other is by (b) skepticism which nullifies the promise’s fulfillment. Fortunately, for our father and mother of the faith, and ultimately for us, the promise was confirmed. Their trust was greatly encouraged by (1) Yahweh’s reminder of His omnipotence: “Is anything too hard for the LORD?” And by (2) the promise being repeated: “I will return to you, according to the time of life, and Sarah will have a son.” Furthermore, the couple’s faith and hope were revitalized by (3) the promise being affirmed by a display of divine insight, convicting Sarah’s conscience and supernaturally displacing her skepticism with the gift of faith: “And He said [to her with directness] nay, but you did laugh.” Sarah was silenced. She perceived that He indeed had accurately searched out the uncertainty of her heart, affirmed His word was true, and that nothing was outside His reach. The fact of her conception is proof of her repentance, forgiveness, and elevated faith. “So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the Word [personal rhema] of God” (Romans 10:8). Point: When praying, dear reader, start listening for the Holy Spirit to address you clearly through the Word. When He does, recognize and believe the exhortation or instructive message, or the personal enlightenment that rises in your spirit, heart, and mind. Yahweh is very good to you, as He was with Abraham and Sarah. And He wants to hear from you daily. So start communicating with your Father and be advanced.

The second faith engagement features Abraham and his Intercession while with Yeshua. The patriarch was endeavoring to honor El Elyon’s directive to “walk before Me and be perfect.” He therefore lived at an elevated spiritual level and experienced a theophany at Mamre–a physical manifestation of pre-incarnate Yeshua. Consequently the narrative is historical, unfolding another incident in the progressive development of divine revelation for Abraham. It is written: “Then the men [the two angels] turned away from there and went toward Sodom…” while Abraham remained standing with Yeshua.

The “father of a multitude of nations,” Abraham, harbored compassionate concern over his wayward nephew, Lot and His family, all of whom lived in Sodom. In fact, Lot had become a leader in the foul, doomed city, but kept his mouth closed concerning his faith in God which he had learned from Abraham and Shem. Like most believers do today, he and went along with the city’s wickedness. Lot desperately needed intercessory prayer. Realizing this great failure, Abraham came near to Yeshua and interceded for his family: “Will you sweep away the righteous with the wicked?” (18:22-23). His persistent prayer was answered. The righteous were delivered from Sodom’s direct destruction, although Lot had compromised his righteousness by moving into Sodom to gain social and material advantages. (13:12). Learn: The result Lot’s spiritual recklessness was the tragic circumstances that came upon his family. The episode teaches us: 1. Don’t give sin an opportunity to (a) seep into and (b) progress in your life. Rather, with steady effort, always maintain your biblical values. Be sure to have godliness grow and bear fruit. 2. Be assured, reader, that judgment will come upon all ungodliness. 3. Finally, is there a wayward “Lot” in your family who needs prayer? If so–PRAY!

Personal Application

The severity of the retribution about to descend on Sodom and Gomorrah, and thoughts about what miserable future could lay in store for the unhappy victims of the forthcoming calamity, filled the patriarch’s mercy motivated heart with anguish. Thus, he “drew near” to Yeshua, both physically and spiritually, trusting for divine acceptance and freedom of expression. Note: The man’s inquiry and plea concerning the fate of the righteous was not based primarily upon the principle of mercy, but rested on the righteousness of the Most High, and how his goodness could be expected to find a way for mercy to triumph over judgment. In the end, the discourse–-prayer should often be a discourse; Abraham received all for which he asked. “And the LORD went His way [vanished]”. Points: 1. Yahweh is open to being approached and entreated as we draw near His Throne of Grace through faith in the blood of our resurrected High Priest, Messiah Yeshua. 2. He is not eager to levy harsh judgments or destruction. 3. He will spare the righteous and repentant. 4. He does what is right for the sake of the individual saint…YOU, and the whole earth. Therefore, readers--with Abraham as your inspiration, I repeat--make up your mind to quicken your faith and persist in daily prayer. In this way you will be inwardly transformed and blessed.

The Third Faith Engagement is featured next in Va Yiera, Part 2. Be sure to meet me there and open your mind and heart to Yahweh’s sacred Word. And by way of your submission you will experience the satisfaction of becoming a changed person. Expect!

Tamid Kadima–Always Forward. Hutch Church. Shalom.

item.title: Contenders Weekly Parsha Points
item.description: Gleaning Torah insights for equipping the Saints for service in these Latter Days
item.content:encoded:
Audio edition of Contenders Weekly Parsha Points on Contender's Voice. For more, visit contendersvoice.com.

Lech Lecha (“Go forth yourself”)

Part 2

Are you an unwavering Irvi?

By bringing Abraham and Sarah to Eretz Yisrael and promising that the land would become the heritage of his generations, God was establishing the promised land as the eternal patrimony of the Israelite people--all twelve tribes, not just one or two. Abraham and Sarah each became an Irvi when they traversed their homeland river and traveled to Canaan. [Irvi means “the other side” in Hebrew.] Once settled, Abraham and Sarah never returned to the land of their origin but remained in Canaan. They were single minded people. Are you also an unwavering Irvi. Have you, blessed reader, left your past worldly life behind in exchange for remaining in the Kingdom of God and contentedly growing in grace, or do you straddle both the old and the new worlds, as do most proclaimers? May those of us who claim Messiah Yeshua as Lord and Savior remember the words of Luke and prosper: “No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back is not fit for the Kingdom of God” (Luke 9:62). And James wrote: “A double minded man is unstable in all his ways.” When we trust Yeshua and sanctify our lives, and cross over to the Kingdom of God and Messiah its Sovereign, we become Irvi too. May we too be immovable and build a blessed legacy for our generations.

Your Spiritual Steps and Stages Insert

“Now the Lord said to Abraham, Go fourth, so Abraham went forth…” Genesis 12:1.

Our Elohim speaks to (communicates with) common people like you and me, and does so audibly, Spirit to spirit, Mind to mind, and Heart to heart, by the Holy Spirit in varying forms. 1 Corinthians 12. He says, “I will guide you in the way of wisdom and lead you in straight paths” (Prov. 4:11). Expect this kind of encounter, reader! Point: For you, He will impart new vision, give fresh hope, inspire faith, bestow important instructions, impart understanding and wisdom, bring encouragement, and give a prophetic word of exhortation for us to convey to another. How wonderful! Learn: Saint, all believers must pass through spiritual stages, or phases, in developing close fellowship with our Good Shepherd and gaining experience with the Holy Spirit. Thus, we need to pay attention to Yahweh’s instructions. Point: Your faith journey is, or should be (1) an upward progression of experience in Spirit and Truth; (2) an ascent toward greater “oneness” with Master Yeshua, (3) a growth in sanctification, and (4) the supernatural transformation of your soul. Hence, seek Him and start looking forward to good things, personal things, to come.

Walk in the Faith Steps of Patriarch Abraham.

Abrahamic Faith lessons are next. Connect them with your own life, goals, and spiritual calling. Leave your old spiritual country, if necessary, and cross over to unreduced, whole Spirit and Torah realities with no parts missing, and seize the following Abrahamic examples. The divine calling which was heard and received by Abraham is a type of the Gospel call which goes forth into the earth for people today. The preached Word must be heard and acted upon by faith. Disobedience, reluctance, and compromise are your enemies. But Abraham is your blessed model. Several essential characteristics of faith that our father Abraham exercised are worthy of our undistracted consideration. First, Abraham’s faith was obedient and produced good works–i.e., action. He called his household together, packed, and departed Haran as soon as he was able. Secondly, as was Noah before him, Abraham was prompt and responded without handwringing, or hesitation to the heavenly directive, or his family’s permission. There is no record of complaint or reluctance as the patriarch put Yahweh’s directive into operation. Thirdly, his faith demonstrated intelligence, vision, and good reasoning. Abraham left behind a dangerous and idol-infested culture, trading it in for the Almighty’s strength, provision, protection, fellowship, love, and elevated calling. That’s wisdom! It is written: “Love not the world [system] neither the things that are in the world” (1 John 2:15). Do not become knit into the evil systems and values of the world. Fourthly, Abraham’s faith was perseverent. He was patient. He was delayed in Haran but not diverted from his journey. Undaunted by the troubles of the road, he did not halt his forward progress but continued even after he and Sarah entered Canaan. Therefore we can declare of Abraham, “...he believed in the Lord; and He reckoned it to him as righteousness (15:2-6). For us: Love the things of the Almighty.

Big Step

“He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit” (Matthew 3:11).

Buckle up, reader. It is written: “For it is by grace you have been saved through faith, and it is the gift of God, not by works, so that no one can boast” (Ephesians 2:8). Faith motivates your first step toward a true encounter with the eternal Creator, Yahweh our Elohim. Yet, subsequent to the New Birth experience there is a very important, spiritual encounter you, even all saints, need to receive, despite the critical naysaying of ill equipped Christ proclaimers. It is the Baptism in the Holy Spirit which is accompanied by the evidence of speaking in other tongues, a personal, Spirit inspired prayer language (Mt. 3:11; Acts 1:8; 2:1-4; 10:46; 19:6; 1 Cor. 12:10-30). The baptism in the Holy Spirit is likened to an immersion resulting in the complete filling and over-flowing of the recipient/believer with the presence and power of the Spirit of Elohim.

Conclusion: Turn the parsha’s truth into action!

Your application: These are the faith characteristics of biblical apostolic discipleship, the life-long school to which you have been clearly called! Adhere to these principles and experience (1) greater spiritual enlightenment, (2) closer friendship-fellowship with Messiah Yeshua, and (3) dis-satisfaction with westernized faith. Furthermore, like father Abraham, cross over to an apostolic commitment and become a Spirit filled Irvi. Understand friend–-faith must be sustained, even renewed each day through prayer, study, worship, and conformity to His blessed instructions all the way to the end of your stay on earth. Yes, endurance is required. It is not the one who starts his or her heaven-ward journey who is recognized and blessed as an overcomer, but the one who remains diligent to Yahweh’s truth and completes the journey. This is not legalism at all. It is love! And dear reader, you are not one who grows weary and turns aside. There is much more we can share about the virtues of Abraham’s life. We will do so next week with Parsha Va Yeira (“He appeared”)

A Poem affirming an unpopular biblical reality!

If faith produces no works to see,

That faith is not a living tree.

Thus faith and works together grow,

A separate life they cannot know,

They are soul and body, head and heart,

What God has joined let no man part. [1]

Abraham did not write this poem. Yet he learned to live by its truth.

Tamid Kadima–Always Forward. Hutch Church, your host. Shalom

1.Leaves of Gold;Bwww.lds.org/gen.Conf./2014/the-cost-and-blessing-of-discipleship/p. Greater Works, S.W.

item.content:encoded:
Audio edition of Contenders Weekly Parsha Points on Contender's Voice. For more, visit contendersvoice.com.

Book of Genesis

Lech Lecha (“Get yourself out”)

Part 1

Did you Know?

“Abram the Hebrew” (Gen. 14:13), referred to as the “father of our faith”, was not justified by faith alone. Are you shocked, dear reader? You shouldn’t be. His faith was made complete, in fact, through righteous acts and timely obedience to Yahweh’s directions to go unto a land he would be shown, and dwell there. Before this event, however, he was a common man who was not morally distinguished but simply lived amidst the polytheistic framework of Mesopotamia. And unlike righteous Noah before him, Abraham was not particularly virtuous either. Nevertheless, he was chosen and directed simply by the grace of God. However, Abraham’s divine summons initiated a profound spiritual transformation that followed His emigration to Canaan and eventually his ascension of Mount Moriah with Isaac, a knife, and a bundle of wood. Point: Though some may regard you and me as less significant than others, Yahweh sees us as pivotal followers of Yeshua who can accomplish much for His glory by abiding in His word and yielding to the Holy Spirit.

Cross Over

Abraham was first called a Hebrew in Genesis 14:13. The word or title “Hebrew” is revealed in Strong’s Heb. 5680 as “iber.” Some scholars believe that “iber” comes from Abraham’s ancestor named Eber. See Genesis 10:21-25. In any case, “iber” is believed to mean “one who has crossed over from the other side.” Notwithstanding, the name means “the man that had come across the water.” And Abraham was that man from the other side that traversed the river Euphrates and then the Jordan to enter Canaan. Hence both Abraham and Sarah, his wife, and Lot also, became “ibers”, or Hebrews. Nevertheless, Hebrew is not a national name for the reason that there was no related nation at the time. Consider: When believers in Yeshua are baptized we cross over and through the water (immersion/baptism), rising from darkness into light, from bondage to freedom from sin to life abundant. John 5:24. [1].

“For I know the plans I have for you…” (Jer. 29:11).

Consider the words of Apostle James, the brother of Yeshua, our blessed Messiah and coming King. He wrote: “In the same way, faith by itself, if it is not accompanied by action (righteous works), is dead” (See James 1:14-24). An “iber” is one who is an ardent doer of the word realizing that faith and action work together. They are partners, my friend. Therefore add to your faith the fruit of the Spirit, and cross over to His undiminished, apostolic transformative “full truth.” No hesitation, which is actually a time frame that will vitiate your initial resolve and cool your zeal. By all means, become an iber.

Friend: Have you elevated yourself yet from being a routine church goer to following Yeshua as a genuine disciple–as his personal apprentice and according to the original, Torah and Glory faith once delivered to the saints? If not, why not? There’s a big difference between the two, you know. Point: Re-consider His words: “If anyone wishes to come after Me, he must deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow Me [i.e., love and obey Me]” (Matthew 16:24). This is His prescription for your life. Are you traversing this blessed narrow road? Or the wide road? Or straddling both as are many saints?

Yeshua: Torah Teacher and Spirit Baptizer

Central Truth: “It is a characteristic of our age that if people want any gods at all, they want them to be gods who do not demand much; comfortable gods, smooth gods who do not rock their “lifestyle” boat but who will pat their heads and scratch their backs. Such folks invoke the name of Jesus [Yeshua] as one who [is] this kind of comfortable god, and therefore listen not to His commandments.. Remember, it was He who said not only should we not break [His] commandments, we should not even think about breaking them. Matthew 5:19 and 1 John 2:4. Sounds too tough for you? Forming your life by Yeshua’s words is crucial for a fruit bearing, upward spiritual journey, friend. The King of Glory does not equivocate or exaggerate. He is forthright and means exactly what He teaches. [1B] “I have come into the world to bear witness to the truth” (John 18:37). Also: “If you love Me, you will keep my commandments” (John 14:15). Only a fool would dismiss this statement.

Be strong and courageous.

Aim: Do not focus on your past, but go forward. Press onward, dear reader, to the place of the inflow of the Spirit, the ground of submission, strength of soul–your heart, mind, will, and temperament. Where is that place? It is here... “only believe.” When you trust Yeshua and His words, and allow Him to take “charge of the situation, whatever that may be, you are absolutely brought into everything that God has, because you dare to follow what He says-- ‘fear not, only believe’ (Mark 5:36. [6B]

Parsha Lech Lecha (“Get yourself out”)

Beresheit 12:1-17:27; Isaiah 40:27-41:16; Matthew 1:22-23; Acts 7:1-8;

Our parsha commentary lesson is Lech [masculine form] Lecha [feminine form]. It translates as “go forth, yourself.” It was said by the prominent Hasidic rabbi, Lubavitcher Rebbe, that Lech Lecha (“Go, to you”)...are among the most important words ever spoken in history. Why? Learn: Because with these words God set Abraham on the course that would reverse the process of spiritual degeneration that humanity had fallen into ever since the expulsion of Adam and Eve from the Garden of Eden. It is the course that would lead it to the giving of the Torah on Mount Sinai, the Savior Himself, the outpouring of the Holy Spirit, and spiritual regeneration of all believers. Note: There is much to read in this parsha. It addresses a number of people and events that shape the narrative of Abraham and Sarah’s migration and settlement in Canaan. We will be most attentive to Abraham’s life.

The Summons

“Now the LORD said to Abram, Go forth from your country, and from your relatives and

from your father’s house, to a land which I will show you; and I will make you a great nation, and I will bless you, and make your name great; and you shall be a blessing; And I shall bless those who bless you,. And the one who curses you I will curse. And in you all the families of the earth will be blessed. So Abram went forth as the LORD had spoken to him…” (B’resheit 12:1-3).

The Almighty’s call to Abraham--a summons that included Sarah, reveals (a) that God watches over everyone, and can call and transform the most unlikely, remote, and even troublesome people. Consider the apostle, Paul. Look at the man who was crucified to the right of Yeshua. Contemplate yourself, reader. Furthermore, in calling Abraham, Yahweh (b) transformed him from being a visionary into becoming His personal emissary, one who could speak with authority concerning the reality, the nearness, and the holy character of the living Elohim. Point: Be sure of this, reader: the development of ongoing spiritual growth and inner transformation for which you hunger progresses only by way of consistent obedience to the Father’s will. The Gospels repeatedly affirm that conformance to known and applicable truth elevates spiritual maturity. And this principle applies to those today who have (1) put their faith in Yeshua the Son, are (2) reborn of His Spirit, and (3) have His Word infused into their minds and written upon the new heart. Note: We are saved by faith alone, not by works. How True. But this statement is true also: We are saved for works…the fruit of the Spirit and that which shows love to our Creator and fellow man. Do you agree, beloved Messiah Follower? Remember, Abraham was called for the purpose of performing designated works.

Equipped

Elohim’s culling [picking out] of Abraham distinguished him forever. The command was authoritative, perhaps even intimidating, but it was accompanied by a number of precious promises; wonderful assurances that more than compensated for the difficulties and labors that the long and arduous journey would visit upon him. The divine summons provided a manifold incentive [uniting various features] and a sustaining measure of cheer for the patriarch--as indicated in Genesis 12. Abraham believed the words of Elohim and “...went forth as Yahweh had spoken…”

Chosen

Abraham was a Chaldean. He alone--of all Terah’s family, of all the descendents, of all the residents of Ur, of all the people on the earth--received a personal summons from the Most High to embark on a physical and spiritual journey, one that would result in the transformation of the spiritual nature of mankind. Noah was alive when the patriarch was born, so was Shem. Hence, from his ancestors Abraham learned about El Shaddai, the Creator and his great works. In all likelihood Abraham spent time reaching out for greater knowledge of the Most High. “...you will find Me when you search for Me…” This scripture is for you, dear reader. Start now!

Tamid Kadima-Always Forward. Hutch Church. Shalom

Lech Lecha–Part Two follows this week. Meet me.

1. Ibid. Adapted; edited: Shedding the veil.

item.content:encoded:
Audio edition of New! Weekly Parsha Points on Contender's Voice. For more, visit contendersvoice.com.

Book of Genesis

Parsha Noach (“Noah”)

Do you have a hero; someone you trust, admire and would like to emulate? If not...

consider Noah.

Note: Our previous lesson, Parsha Beresheit, opened the new year of the Torah reading cycle. In it we featured 4 types–or symbolic representations, of Messiah Yeshua. The parshas give readers a fundamental way to learn the Torah Israelite history, and Hebraic values. Fifty-four instructive parshas are included in the 52 week reading cycle. This week’s lesson is Parsha Noach which highlights the faith and character of Noah for the readers to evaluate and admire. By the way, the yearly Torah chronological reading sequence was started by Ezra in the fourth century, before Yeshua’s birth in Bethlehem. Point: Reader, whoever you are, make sure your spiritual transformation, which will produce affirmative changes in your life, continues with refreshed zeal by imbibing the Scriptures regarding righteous Noah. It is written: “And God said unto Noah…make thee an ark of gopher wood…” (Gen. 6:13-14). Noah, we are sure, was given a detailed blueprint for constructing the enormous wooden ship, along with an impartation of wisdom to bring the craft to perfection. Workmanship flaws would prove to be fatal during the long and tumultuous voyage.

Particulars and Details

We would imagine the enormous task was overwhelming at first, but demanding from start to finish. However Noah, though not a perfect human, was nevertheless not a man who would dilly-dally in response to a divine edict. Once He heard the decree from God He went right to work. Details were of utmost importance. Two or three haphazardly pegged planks could give way over time to surging water pressure, and allow untold volumes of sea water to flood the ship, and cause it to roll over. In any case, Noah is the faithful, dependable workman Yahweh has exhibited whereby observant believers can strive to emulate. Six standards Noah met successfully. They pertain to you: 1. Take on the commitment of changing your life, reader. 2. Do not tarry, vacillate, or compromise. Those are your enemies. 3. Strive to become like the ship builder as you construct your life and legacy also according to Yahweh’s detailed scriptural blueprint. No more shortcuts. 4. Pray and recharge your faith battery daily and proceed with your particular service! And succeed! As you go, do not dismiss the less notable particulars embedded in His commandments. 5. Take His whole Word to heart and reach your assigned destination as an overcomer. 6. Finally, fulfill your responsibilities even if they seem bewildering, enormous, and demanding. So what? Keep his Word and prosper! You too can succeed.

Parsha Noach (“Noah”)

References: Genesis 6:9-11:32; Isaiah 54:1-55:5; Acts 1:1-11; 1 Peter 3:18-22.

Parsha Noach starts with this: “These are the records of the generations of Noah. He

was a righteous man, blameless among the people of his time; Noah walked with God”

(Beresheit 6:9). Noah walked with God and kept himself away from the mounting moral evil of his wicked society (6:9-8:22). Thus he found favor with God. Yet, from the time of Adam to that of Noah, mankind had ventured for centuries downhill into increasing sinfulness until at last divine judgement was decreed on the widespread lawlessness of human societies.

Leakproof Boat

Noah [Noach in Hebrew] means “rest.” He was obviously a just man before his Maker. The man of faith had a sincere and upright heart, and was trusting in the promise of the Seed of the Woman…the appearance on earth of a heaven-sent Redeemer. Consequently, humanity could not be totally eliminated. Thus, a remnant would need to be sustained. Hence, God spoke to Noah, saying, “...the end of all flesh has come before Me” (verse 6:13). Note: YHWH was not seeking the ruination of mankind, but the wicked, injurious and totally corrupt condition of human society had risen as an unrelenting stench into the face of the Almighty with such persistence and volume that the flood remedy could no longer be delayed.

Lawlessness reigns.

The earth, referring to humans along with the hybrid descendants of other dimensional entities, had become wholly defiled, filled with unspeakable violence, and lacking in any redeemable qualities. Verse 6:12. Judgment was promised. The universal, supernaturally wrought destruction of unrepentant man, monstrous creatures, beasts, and giants as well, was declared and the cleansing of the defiled lands would occur. Still, YHWH remembered the righteous–-the clean and blameless amidst the debauchery, and He commissioned Noah…”Make thee an ark.” The work would be a test of enduring faith that would produce the means of salvation. So Noah, threatened for decades by lawless humans, the violence of Nephilim beings, rampant anarchy, and pressed by the threat of a coming flood, continued building and also preaching by faith inspired obedience . Consider: Four pertinent points showing us that obedience to Yahweh’s commandments always results in success. Furthermore, Noah’s willing conformance represents the purest and foremost expression of faith, love, and of chaste worship. Would this standard characterize the westernized American Church? Ot you? Be honest.

1. Then the LORD said to Noah, “Make thee an ark...” ( 6:14). Not knowing what would unfold, Noah followed the blueprint and went about building the Ark, a typical representation of our refuge in the storm, Messiah Yeshua.

2. Then the LORD said, “Come thou…into the ark...” (7:1). Noah and his family entered the well-stocked Ark, along with the animals, through its single door. This reminds us that there is only one door to the Kingdom of God, and it is Yeshua.

3. Then the LORD remembered Noah and said, “Go forth from the ark...” (8:16). Noah

et al left the ark and entered a brand new world, much different from the one his family had left behind. When we come to Yeshua, we enter a completely different world, the Kingdom of God, and stand poised for the threshold of the New earth and Heaven.

4. Then Noah built an altar on the earth and presented a burnt offering, sanctifying it

and inaugurating the Noahic Covenant and its seven laws for mankind. Note: Religious life is acceptable with Yahweh our Elohim when it establishes a holy union between God and man and acknowledges His grace and authority.

Summed

The Tower of Babel, Shem’s prominence, the genealogy of promise, and other items of interest follow. Though most of our post’s attention has been on Noah, we will also look at the Noahic Covenant.

Watchman Insert: The Noahic Covenant. Genesis 9:1-17.

Yahweh blessed Noah and his family, and made a covenant with him called the Noahic Covenant. It was a covenant for human kind accompanied by a sacrifice and attested to by the appearance of a rainbow. The Noahic Covenant, sanctioned the repopulation of the earth, eating animal flesh, protection of human life by judicially declaring it sacrosanct, execution as the punishment for murder [a capital crime], and the institution of human government for societal order. Summarily, it provided divine permission and endorsement for the increase, protection, and sustenance of the human family, and affirmed Yahweh’s care and goodness for mankind. Point: We learn from parsha Noach that the Almighty’s grace is revealed in many ways including (1) His dealing with fallen man by way of covenant, (2) His adherence to His covenant despite the sinfulness and unfaithfulness of man, and (3) His enduring oversight of redeemed man being placed under a Kingdom government of mercy and grace.

The Noahic Covenant as the religious foundation of the NWO government !!?

Sound the Shofar: The cat’s out of the bag! Israel, America, and other nations are pushing for the Noahic Covenant to become internationally accepted as the moral code for all nations and used for uniting the world religions. The covenant framework has been endorsed by Congress, is recognized favorably by the UN, and codified in the Jewish Talmud–an uninspired commentary compiled by men. Noahic Law is viewed as binding on all humanity. However, the Covenant, once formally accepted as the moral paradigm for human societies, will become interwoven with legal prohibitions and variations, geopolitical laws and various amended religious doctrines. Furthermore, penal code and enforcements esteemed appropriate by the joined nations will be adjudicated by Rabbinic interpretation and a Sanhedrin seated in Jerusalem. Point: The Noahic Covenant, shuffled into the NWO antichrist government would form a hybrid government overseen by Israel and a restored rabbinic Sanhedrin. In other words, such a government would not be “Jesus friendly.”

Watchmen on the wall are raising their voices. Christianity and the acknowledgment of Jesus Christ as Lord and Savior could, in time, be interpreted as idolatry and a violation of a compromised application of the Noahic Covenant. In other words, expressed faith in Yeshua as the Messiah could become interpreted as a capital crime, along with Bible based worship. Such would be interpreted as idolatry. Point: Remain prayerful and discerning. As it is written: “If the world hates you, keep in mind that they hated me first…” (John 15: 18).

Noah, a righteous man whose uncompromising character was not shaped by the world

around him or by his contemporaries. His life teaches today’s attentive, enthusiastic Christians profound truths to conceive. I’ve included just three:

1. It is possible to be righteous and pure of heart in an unclean, lawless society.

2. Only the person who is in close, regular communion with YHWH, by conforming to His sacred instructions, will not be overcome by a wicked age or tricked by misinterpretations of Scripture.

3. Faith is not alive and present where obedience to the Word of God is absent. Pious Noah was prompt in his obedience to follow LORD’s call and detailed instructions.

Let’s grow up in the LORD

Yeshua declared: “If I be lifted up from the earth, I will draw all men unto me” (John 12:32). These “all men” are called to be disciples--students and followers of the Messiah; apprentices in His “school of faith”. Build your faith on these critical points and always keep them in mind: A. Yeshua, is the High Priest of our discipleship. B. The Torah is the standard of discipleship. C. And we are sealed by the Holy Spirit, who is the power of our discipleship. D. And overcoming obstacles and maturing in the likeness of Yeshua our Adonai is the outcome of your discipleship.

Your Personal Application: “Now Elohim has not only raised up the Lord, but will also raise us up through His power” (1 Corinthians 6:14). The great guidance factor in the lives of believers is not our personal needs or wants, not even the needs of others, or those of worthwhile organizations. The sign posts of life and service are the commandments of our Redeemer and Master---Yeshua Ha Mashiach. Our goal is to become true disciples; unhesitant doers of the Word as was our parsha hero, Noah; believers who are true to His plan and purpose become equipped with the Spirit and Torah to participate in them. Finally, get baptized with the Holy Spirit. You can experience this, even today! Pray. Expect. It is an important step in your transformation.

Tamid Kadima-Always Forward. Hutch Church. Shalom. Parsha Lech Lecha is next. Abraham and Sarah are featured therein

item.content:encoded:
Audio edition of NEW! Weekly Parsha Points on Contender's Voice. For more, visit contendersvoice.com.

Parsha Beresheit (“Beginning”)

References: Genesis 1:1-6:8; Isaiah 42:5-43:10; John 1:1-5.

“What has been will be again; there is nothing new under the sun” (Eccl. 1:9).

Question: Reader, what similar tasks do you and Adam and Eve have in common? Answer: They were instructed to keep the Garden, multiply descendants, and restore the worship of Yahweh to the earth. They failed. Yeshua, the second Adam, did not fail in His divine assignment. Hence, believers are also instructed. We are expected to contend for the whole Word of God, multiply disciples, and restore the original Torah-based, apostolic worship taught and modeled by Yeshua, the twelve Apostles, and followed by His Nazarene disciples. Do you envision this for your life as a disciple? If not, be bold and become a full fledged radical. Obey His commandments, all that are known, pertinent, and doable, and move on to know the Almighty more intimately.

Catch a “Second Wind”

This prophecy is written especially for readers who have served Yeshua with forbearance but are now stalled: “Let us not become weary in doing good, for at the proper time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up” (Gal. 6:9). A fresh commitment would lead you, dear reader, to the threshold of a dynamic new beginning. Follow through! Rising and going forward will (a) uplift and empower your walk of faith and definitely (b) expand your prophetic vision. Pray and listen carefully for your Good Shepherd’s voice. He still speaks. Further, develop a closer fellowship with Him by the communion of the Holy Spirit. You are indeed chosen to be among His Latter Day elect. Therefore, continue forward in His Kingdom, commit to read through His sacred words. John 14:26; 2 Corinthians 13:14; Revelation 19:7. Ask to see His glory!

“For by grace you have been saved through faith…” (Ephesians 2:8).

There is a spiritual richness in parsha Beresheit to comment upon in this first post. However, we cannot address and evaluate every aspect of the narrative. Therefore, I have chosen to single out and focus on Messiah Yeshua–where He is revealed and how that relates to you and me. Of Him it is written: “In the beginning was the Word [He was not created nor did he begin to be], and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. He was in the beginning with God. All things came into being through Him” (John 1:1-3). Let’s stare at Him and view His holy realities, beautiful character, his righteous life, servanthood, and more--and be inspired, and even become truly zealous in our discipleship journey through life. Let’s gaze through the lattice at the Messiah.

Imitate His humility. Model His obedience! .

First: “And being found in appearance as a man, He humbled himself and became obedient to death; even death on a cross” (Phil.2:8). Yeshua exemplified obedience. While living sinless in a fallen and corrupt world Yeshua remained obedient to His Father’s Word, even to the point of enduring an excruciating death on a cross. Apart from His willingness to do His Father’s will you and I would still captives of sin and darkness.

Second: “Jesus replied and said, blessed are those who hear the Word of God and obey it” (Luke 11:28). Yeshua complied with the will of His heavenly Father and following the His resurrection was blessed beyond measure and given all authority in heaven and earth. He’s the King of kings and we, His servants, must decide once for all if we will indeed obey the King’s edicts. It appears modern Church-goers do not. I think American saints need to (1) learn the “fear of the Lord” and (2) honor His commandments. What’s more, believers must (3) recover and embrace the sanctioned apostolic Spirit and Torah rooted faith if we expect to experience intimate friendship fellowship with Him and undergo a progressive personal transformation of heart, mind, and will that carries us into harmony with His prophetic vision. This is the sanctified path to follow friends, if you want to grow into the person you want to be.

Point: Since the eternal Son, Yeshua of Judah and the House of David, obeyed the Torah perfectly and followed without hesitation the instructions of His heavenly Father, let’s draw close and gaze at His beauty. Yes, He is risen and abides as our High Priest before the Throne of Grace. Because of Yeshua’s unflawed conformance to the sacred Law, God exalted Him. He is the King of Glory, Lord of lords, the Judge of the living and the dead, and the One who separates the sheep from the goats. He is not the domesticated, non-confrontational, westernized Christ modern Christian culture promotes today. “Who is this King of Glory? The LORD strong and mighty, the LORD mighty in battle” (Psalm 24:8). Your directive: Yeshua is Adonai, the powerful and authoritative, righteous Son of God, who, on the cross, put an end to sin and spoiled principalities and powers. He deserves to be loved, honored, reverenced, and obeyed. Cast away the decaying notion that conforming one’s life to Scripture’s truth is legalism.

Whoever you are, “...ask for the ancient paths…” and return to them (Jeremiah 6:16).

Yeshua, your High Priest, is an eternal Being--deity existing in a continuous state. He is the divine One in Whom is the Life, and Light is the emanation of that Life. He was the Word of God before His incarnation as man. “In the beginning…” all things were created by Him. Colossians 1:16-20. Today, as you know, Yeshua is currently gathering and restoring His Torah to the lost sheep of the House of Israel...one converted and redeemed person at a time. Yes, the Father has provided a new beginning for fallen mankind and now for His scattered tribes. That’s our Messiah’s compassionate work and He is revealed in numerous types throughout the book of Genesis. We will be highly inspired to bond with Him more closely than before as we peer through the lattice and view Yeshua in the four types revealed by parsha Beresheit. Solomon 2:9-13.

Type 1

Yeshua is the Beginning. “In the beginning God [Elohim] created the heavens and the earth.” (Genesis 1:1). Yeshua is seen as the beginning. “In the beginning was the Word [He was not created, nor did he begin to be], and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. He was in the beginning with God. All things came into being through Him…’ (John 1:1-3). To emphasize again, Yeshua is an Eternal Being, deity existing in a continuous state. He was the Word before He became man. “In the beginning…” all things were created by Him. There was a beginning of creation, and only Yahweh our Elohim was before it. What does this mean to you? By faith in Yeshua saints become new creations! Yahweh has an order. Disorder and chaos–that which is not His will but the product of sin–are never the beginning of things but are only permitted until His restoration–that which is very good–has all things returned to their ordered and useful place. To that end, the brooding, hovering, and vitalizing presence of the Spirit moved over the chaotic deep, and God spoke, “Let there be light….” And you also were moved upon by the Spirit to see Yeshua…and the new you was miraculously and powerfully made into a new creation in Him. Rejoice!

Type 2

Yeshua is the Creator. “In the beginning God created…” (Genesis 1:1). Paul’s epistle speaks of the Son in this way: “For by Him were all things created, both in the heavens and in the earth, visible and invisible…all things have been created through Him and for Him (Colossians 1:15-16). The entire universe--every galaxy, system, star, planet, moon, molecule, atom, particle, electron, neutron, quark, and string vibe; everything organic or inorganic, material or non material–are all held together and sustained, each in its duration, sphere, and purpose by Yeshua’s power! Everything visible and invisible, including principalities and rulers of spiritual darkness, and all energy, in the far flung cosmos is subject to His authority. Think about that! What does this mean to you? It’s obvious! He is well able to fulfill His promises and do great and marvelous things in the lives of them who trust Him. His eyes are always upon you and He hears your prayers. Learn: Only He can bring out the best in you, attentive reader. Become His front row student!

Type 3

Yeshua is the Seed. It is written: “And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed. He shall bruise [crush] you on the head, and you shall bruise Him on the heel” (Genesis 3:15). This Scripture in Beresheit is called the protoevangelium. It is the first declaration of the Gospel. Yeshua is seen as the seed of the woman that will defeat Satan and redeem humanity. He was born of a virgin, lived in perfect obedience to the Torah–the Law of Moses, and made atonement for believing mankind by His cross and resurrection. Should not Spirit and Torah ministries of Yahweh be restored to all His varied people? Absolutely! And it is happening as you read! Torah perfection and Spirit fullness are united in Yeshua. What does this mean to you? You are in the family line of those who have placed their faith in the shed blood of the Seed of the woman--the Lamb of God, Yeshua HaMashiach. Let the Torah and the Holy Spirit be united and operative in you as it was in Him and also the original apostolic Torah and Spirit faith!

Type 4

Yeshua is the Light. “The earth was formless and void, and darkness was over the surface of the deep, and the spirit of Elohim was moving over the surface of the waters. Then Elohim said, ‘Let there be light,’ and there was light” (Genesis 1:1-2). Yeshua is seen as the Light. The Hebrew word for light is “or”. It means to illuminate, dispel darkness and establish clarity and order. [2] It is written: “All things were made through him…in Him was life, and the life was the light of men. And the light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not overcome it” (John 1:3-5). He is the Light that brings knowledge, purity and reveals the presence of God. What does this mean to you? His Word and Light are within you by the Holy Spirit. You are thus His light with a recreated spirit by the New Birth. Hence, He declares this word to you, blessed reader: “You are the light of the world–a city on a hilltop that cannot be hidden…Let your good deeds shine out for all to see” (See Matthew 5:1-16). Therefore, take your lamp out of the closet, if its there, and enlighten others by walking in His light before them. Be come more than a convert, become a disciple.

Your Personal Application

“It must be seen as a matter of great importance to God that His messianic covenant people, Jew, Gentile, Christian, and you, have been justified by faith alone in Messiah Yeshua resulting in a miraculous, life-changing spiritual birth. Believer, you can wallow in a fallen, corrupted world that lies under the power of Satan or you can live everyday under the Holy Spirit’s power and authority and abide daily with Messiah! You have been divinely empowered to walk in compliance to God’s moral standards and sacred instructions…the good path of obedience spoken of by Jeremiah. Understand: In John 14:15-24 Yeshua stresses four times that there exists an essential relationship between (1) loving Him and (2) obeying what He has commanded. Point: Again, for His supreme faith-life YOU have been spiritually reborn and empowered by the Holy Spirit. So walk it out successfully. You can do this! It has been His plan for His saints from “in the beginning,” from the point of creating heaven and earth, and, as I have pointed out, you were known even then! His place for you in restoring His whole truth is very important. Therefore, go beyond conversion and pew-sitting and venture into genuine messianic discipleship. Fellowship with His devoted, elevated students–the ones who follow the Good Shepherd. Hear and obey His voice, and prosper in your spirit, soul, and life. [3]

Tamid Kadima-Always Forward. Hutch Church. Parsha Noach is next.

Edited: 1.52 Hebrew words, p. 89; D. Adamson. 2. Leaves of Gold; Hannah More, p. 180. 3. ESV Study Version Biblical Ethics; P. 2535. All Adapted and rewritten

item.title: NEW! Contenders Voice Weekly Parsha Points
item.description: Gleaning Torah insights for equipping the Saints for service in these Latter Days.
item.content:encoded:
Audio edition of NEW! Contenders Voice Weekly Parsha Points on Contender's Voice. For more, visit contendersvoice.com.

Genesis Parsha: Beresheit (“In the Beginning”)

Genesis 1:1-6:8; Isaiah 42:5-43:10; John 1:1-5.

Caution: If you are expecting to read a nice, comfortable, non-confrontational parsha review, you better buckle up!!

Comment: Westernized Christianity has devolved over time in response to imbibing new knowledge. Embracing a conflicting host of unbiblical standards has reduced the integrity and spiritual power of the modern Church. Our hope of restoring spiritual power and whole truth is not at all connected to gaining new knowledge.

Restoration: It’s connected to believers returning to and recovering old knowledge.

Our Need is a New Beginning

It is written: “In the beginning God created heaven and earth” (Genesis 1:1). We read this statement with a sense of wonder. Readers realize at once that the Creator, Yahweh our Elohim, has incomprehensible power, authority, wisdom, and faithfulness. He also possesses agape love for His children. It is a holy covenant love that is pure, selfless, enduring and powerful. Hence, when there seems to be no way for you or me to prevail over life’s hostile circumstances and the world’s ubiquitous spiritual wickedness, we remember His Word: “Behold, I am the LORD, the God of all flesh. Is there anything too hard for Me” (Jeremiah 32:27). No! Of course not. So, we call out knowing He will hear, stretch out His arm, and make a way where before, there was no way! Point: There is no need in your life, dear friend, that lies beyond His love, reach, or creative power. Hence, if you’re mired in spiritual dormancy, as many saints are today, seek Yahweh to uplift and inspire you with a new beginning in your faith life.

Parsha Beresheit confirms the importance of “new beginnings.”

You and I, dear reader, are losing an existential conflict with a ruthless adversary--lawlessness. It affects us, our families, and the whole nation! To turn the tables on this struggle, the core foundations of biblical faith that have fallen must be restored and honored. Lawlessness is sinfulness, and it has completely preempted our social order and is the contagious plague that now reigns throughout our nation’s spiritual and secular institutions. Point: The original apostolic faith and practice is the powerful unsullied Torah and Spirit-led faith which was in place at the beginning of the New Covenant. This heavenly sanctioned faith has become compromised, vitiated, and even disfigured over the centuries. But by the grace of God that faith “once delivered” is gradually being restored. Consequently, a widespread revival and a third great spiritual awakening are now within reach. But Yeshua’s people must repent and galvanize an actual “new beginning” by taking hold of and restoring that N.T. orthodoxy which existed in the beginning. Recover and follow His instructions.

The fruit of an infernal spell.

Prophecy News Network reported recently that many churches today are flying rainbow flags in their sanctuaries. Their pastors preach in Pride-colored vestments. Queer hymns and transgender themes, and other such abominations are also featured. What’s more, rainbow colored bread has been used for Holy Communion. This is what has happened to the pure, Apostolic faith taught and modeled by Messiah Yeshua, His twelve apostles, and Nazarene followers. What does this mean to you, reader? It is written: “Come out of her [Babylonian spirituality], my people, so that you will not share in her sins or contract any of her plagues” (Rev. 18:4). In other words, believers should turn around and go back to His words of life, abide in them, and build their legacies.

Our corrupt culture has invaded the institutional Church.

The intrusion of worldly values into westernized Christianity is blasphemy arrogantly displayed! Do you want to live where the Scriptures have been compromised, even mocked? For example, what happened to the Sabbath? And where are the Christian men? Female pastors and preachers are ascending to fill the gap. This is a predictable phenomenon which the weight of Scripture does not support. Yet many are prominent in the pulpits who endorse abortion, divergence from the Scriptures and support unbiblical promotions of the feminist movement. Then there are many fathers who will not take a spiritual leadership role in the family. Take to heart: This evil spiritual devolution has been spawned from the dark, infernal regions and is undergirded by unrelenting demonic power and energy. But such dark spiritual forces can be defeated, and will be, but the saints must return to their place of strength for an enduring new beginning. Old knowledge—remember? This would be the original Nazarene, apostolic faith handed down to the saints Point: In this dark hour almost every believer needs to throw off their old compromised wineskins, stand with fresh prophetic vision, and lay hold of a “new beginning”. View it in Jeremiah 6:16. It is a summons to a return to the ancient paths and walk in them.

Turn around! Honor all known and doable sacred truth!

Our warfare is spiritual. Dedicated warriors, those who reject the notion that obedience is legalism and something only for ancient Israel but not the Church, are needed. If wickedness is not confronted and overcome it just increases and causes more heartache, personal distress, social destruction, and judgment--just as we are witnessing in America today. Folks, the ongoing passivity among the saints is simply unacceptable. Point: You and I cannot be true disciples of the Messiah if we grieve the Spirit by shunning the Father’s words and turning from the Son’s Torah-based ways. If we won’t repent but continue instead to brush off the vitality and duty [responsibility] of obeying to His applicable and doable commandments, we will lose our nation, freedom, our own personal destiny--and they will not be retrievable.

The enemy is exposed. Resist. You are a guardian of His truth.

Consider: Blatant disregard for obeying Yahweh’s commandments is the mark of a lazy, undisciplined saint. Sadly, it’s widespread. (1) Spiritual waywardness, (2) adhering to false doctrines, and (3) backsliding continue to move Americans deeper into the realm of divine judgment. Point: Reader, make Yeshua’s holy, Torah-based teaching direct the course of your life. Pray and study! Allow the Spirit to impart wisdom and stir up holy zeal in you. Turn, if you must, from the worldly ways of mixed, compromised faith. Journey on the ancient paths and begin your radical heart, mind-and temperament transformation into the strong overcomer the Almighty has destined you to become. Recovering the Torah and Spirit faith taught by Yeshua and His apostles is the New Beginning we need. It is the only way. No more compromise. Its an enemy.

Torah is the foundation of your New Beginning

The central truth of Genesis is the failure and weakness of mankind and how it is overcome by the redeeming grace of the Holy One of Israel. God is sovereign and well able and willing to provide and sustain a “new beginning” for you, reader. Here is your primary directive: “This is the will of God, your sanctification” (1 Thess. 4:3). Point: Re-charge your faith journey with a fresh commitment, a fresh start characterized by a full compliance to His instructions. In other words, dear reader–give your whole life the “new beginning” of which we have spoken. Dear reader, you simply cannot fulfill your divinely assigned, end days destiny apart from compliance to all His words. Also, be accompanied by the Spirit and angelic escorts through your life of service and fellowship with King Yeshua. This the only way of fulfilling you God-given destiny.

Get ready. Put on your reading glasses.

Part One is concluded. Part two is right behind. Look for it tomorrow. Part Two is shorter but it highlights Yeshua and provides four personal applications for you drawn from Parsha Beresheit . You are a blessing and very much appreciated!! Thank you for coming aboard. Room is being made for your comments and inquiries.

Tamid Kadima-Always Forward. Hutch Church. I will join you at Part two.

item.title: To “Contend” for His truth is essential; it is the summons that distinguishes this pivotal era from the others:
item.description: “...earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered to the saints…” (Jude 1:3).
item.content:encoded:
Audio edition of To “Contend” for His truth is essential; it is the summons that distinguishes this pivotal era from the others: on Contender's Voice. For more, visit contendersvoice.com.

Recovering Biblical Truth

“And thou shalt return unto YHWH your Elohim, and shalt obey His voice...” (See Deut. 30:1-10). 2.5 Minutes

While upon Earth, Yeshua--the eternal Son of Yahweh, was a Jewish teacher who expounded the truth and modeled the application of the Torah. He instructed His listeners to honor the Law of Moses and proclaimed the Gospel of the Kingdom of Elohim in the power of the Holy Spirit. Thus the Gospel originated in Israel, was Torah-based, and from there spread throughout the world. As it advanced through the nations, however, it became further and further alienated from its Hebrew-Jewish foundations, the Torah, and Israelite culture. As a result one could say that the original Nazarene Gospel--the unadulterated faith and practice of the Apostles and early disciples, has been in exile for at length. How is that, you ask? Over the centuries institutional, westernized Christianity has taken on markedly divergent expressions of belief and custom, and hence has distanced itself from the unchanging fullness of the sacred Torah-based Word of God. In doing so the nation’s traditional faith has also become emotionally and functionally disconnected from the Gospel’s Hebraic-Jewish traditions not completely identified with its Torah honoring Messiah.

Yet grace abounds. In the last century as the Jews have been returning to the land of Israel, the Holy Spirit has been moving upon them individually and an increasing number of Jewish people are recognizing Yeshua, the “son” of Joseph, as their prophesied Messiah. Consequently the Gospel is being reunited more directly with (a) the Promised Land, (b) the Torah, and (c) its real Jewish--Israelite Messiah, Yeshua of Nazareth. Also, the full ministry of the Holy Spirit is beginning to be recognized as needed as well. This restoration phenomenon is an end-time work of Yahweh’s compassion and grace stirring repentance from lawlessness and a return to heart-felt conformity to sacred truth, i.e.--heart-felt adherence to all known and applicable life instructions. The change of heart needed for such a turn around has been made possible through (1) saving faith in Yeshua and the (2) unspeakably wondrous gift of the Holy Spirit given to indwell the born-again saint. This is a purpose of the blessed New Covenant. And concurrent with its divinely imparted blessings is the (3) infusion of the three enduing virtues: They are faith--which unites the saints to Messiah and eternal life, hope--which lights up the present by brightening the future with Yahweh’s promises--prospects which cheer the believing soul, and love--for God and humanity that elevates, purifies, and brings forth the purest blessings of which this life on earth is capable of bearing. [1] Such is the fruit of “belief” that is based in the Elohim of Israel as He is revealed in the Scriptures. We must return to the “...faith once for all entrusted to the early followers” of Messiah Yeshua.
